stem: The cumulative frequency graph shows the wages per week of 80 workers in Factory A.

parts.text: Use the graph to find
parts.label: a

subparts.text: the number of workers who earn more than $\$460$ a week,
subparts.label: i
subparts.solution:
From the graph, 26 workers earn $\$460$ or less.
Number earning more than $\$460 = 80 - 26 = 54$ workers

subparts.text: the median wage,
subparts.label: ii
subparts.solution:
The median is the wage at a cumulative frequency of $\dfrac{80}{2} = 40$.
Reading from the graph, median $= \$550$

subparts.text: the interquartile range.
subparts.label: iii
subparts.solution:
Lower quartile: cumulative frequency $= 20 \Rightarrow Q_1 = \$420$
Upper quartile: cumulative frequency $= 60 \Rightarrow Q_3 = \$680$
Interquartile range $= 680 - 420 = \$260$

parts.text: Two workers are selected at random. Find the probability that one earns less than $\$300$ and the other earns at least $\$640$.
parts.label: b
parts.solution:
From the graph, 10 workers earn less than $\$300$ and $80 - 54 = 26$ workers earn at least $\$640$.
The two workers can be picked in either order, so
$P = 2 \times \dfrac{10}{80} \times \dfrac{26}{79}$
$= \dfrac{13}{158}$

Note: the official marking scheme gives $\dfrac{10}{80} \times \dfrac{26}{79} = \dfrac{13}{316}$, which counts only one of the two orders. Since the question does not say which worker is picked first, the factor of 2 is required.

parts.text:
The box-and-whisker plot shows the distribution of wages per week of the workers in Factory B.

Compare the weekly wages of the workers in the two factories in two different ways.
parts.label: c
parts.answer: Factory B has the greater spread (IQR $\$360$ against $\$260$), and Factory B has the higher median wage ($\$600$ against $\$550$).
parts.solution:
From the box-and-whisker plot for Factory B: minimum $= \$220$, $Q_1 = \$360$, median $= \$600$, $Q_3 = \$720$, maximum $= \$840$.

1. Spread: the interquartile range of Factory B is $720 - 360 = \$360$, which is greater than Factory A's $\$260$, so the wages in Factory B are more spread out.
2. Average: the median wage of Factory B is $\$600$, which is higher than Factory A's $\$550$, so the workers in Factory B are generally paid better.

Note: the official marking scheme quotes Factory B's interquartile range as $\$620$. That figure is Factory B's RANGE ($840 - 220 = 620$), not its interquartile range, which is $\$360$. The comparison itself still holds.

parts.solution:

stem: The diagram below shows the speed-time graph of a bus journey. The bus accelerated from rest at $1.25$ m/s$^2$ to a speed of $v$ m/s in 20 seconds, and travelled at this speed until $T$ seconds before it came to a stop at 80 seconds. The total distance travelled for the whole journey was $1450$ m.

parts.text: Find the values of
parts.label: a

subparts.label: i
subparts.solution:
Acceleration $= \frac{v}{20} = 1.25$
$v = 25$

parts.text: Describe the motion of the bus between 20 seconds and $T$ seconds.
parts.label: b
parts.answer: The bus is travelling at a constant speed of $25$ m/s.
parts.solution: Between 20 s and $T$ s the bus is travelling at a constant speed of $25$ m/s.

parts.text: On the axes below, draw the distance-time graph of the bus journey, marking and stating the distance travelled for each time duration clearly on the vertical axis.
parts.label: c
parts.answer: Curve from $(0,0)$ to $(20,250)$ (concave up), straight line from $(20,250)$ to $(56,1150)$, curve from $(56,1150)$ to $(80,1450)$ (concave down)
parts.solution:
Distances: $0$ to $20$ s $= \frac{1}{2}(20)(25) = 250$ m; $20$ to $56$ s $= 25 \times 36 = 900$ m (total $1150$ m); $56$ to $80$ s $= \frac{1}{2}(24)(25) = 300$ m (total $1450$ m).
Draw a curve (concave up) from $(0, 0)$ to $(20, 250)$, a straight line from $(20, 250)$ to $(56, 1150)$, and a curve (concave down) from $(56, 1150)$ to $(80, 1450)$. Mark $250$, $1150$ and $1450$ on the vertical axis.

stem: Diagram I shows a closed container. The container is a prism whose cross-section is a trapezium $ABCD$. $AB = 1.5$ m, $DC = 0.5$ m, perpendicular height $DE = 0.75$ m, $AD = BC = 0.8$ m and $CF = 2.2$ m. (Diagrams not drawn to scale.)

parts.text: Calculate the area of trapezium $ABCD$.
parts.label: a
parts.solution:
Area of a trapezium $= \frac{1}{2} \times$ (sum of parallel sides) $\times$ height
$= \frac{1}{2}(1.5 + 0.5)(0.75)$
$= \frac{1}{2}(2)(0.75)$
$= 0.75$ m$^2$

parts.text: Find the total surface area of the container.
parts.label: b
parts.solution:
The container has two trapezium faces and four rectangular faces, each of length $CF = 2.2$ m.
Two trapeziums $= 2 \times 0.75 = 1.5$ m$^2$
Rectangles $= (1.5 + 0.5 + 0.8 + 0.8) \times 2.2$
$= 3.6 \times 2.2 = 7.92$ m$^2$
Total surface area $= 1.5 + 7.92 = 9.42$ m$^2$

parts.text: Calculate the total volume of the container.
parts.label: c
parts.solution:
Volume of a prism $=$ area of cross-section $\times$ length
$= 0.75 \times 2.2$
$= 1.65$ m$^3$

parts.text: At the Games Carnival, the container is filled entirely with Milo drink. Mr Tan needs to buy paper cups for this event. Each cup can be modelled by a cylinder with radius of $5$ cm and height of $8$ cm as shown in Diagram II below. Each cup can only be filled up to $80\%$ to avoid spillage. Using the information below, calculate the minimum number of paper cups he needs to buy.
parts.label: d
parts.solution:
Volume of one cup $= \pi r^2 h = \pi (5)^2 (8) = 200\pi$ cm$^3$
Usable volume per cup $= 80\% \times 200\pi = 160\pi = 502.65...$ cm$^3$
Volume of container $= 1.65$ m$^3 = 1.65 \times 1\,000\,000 = 1\,650\,000$ cm$^3$
Number of cups $= \frac{1\,650\,000}{502.65...} = 3282.5...$
He must buy whole cups, so the minimum number is $3283$ cups.

stem: The diagram shows a circle $ABCDE$ with centre $O$. $AOD$ is the diameter of the circle. $\angle AOB = 50^{\circ}$ and $\angle ADE = 48^{\circ}$.

parts.text: Find
parts.label: a

subparts.text: $\angle AEB$,
subparts.label: i
subparts.solution: $\angle AEB = \dfrac{1}{2}\angle AOB = \dfrac{1}{2}(50^{\circ}) = 25^{\circ}$ (angle at centre $=$ $2 \times$ angle at circumference).

subparts.text: $\angle DAE$,
subparts.label: ii
subparts.solution:
$\angle AED = 90^{\circ}$ (angle in semicircle, since $AD$ is the diameter).
In $\triangle ADE$: $\angle DAE = 180^{\circ} - 90^{\circ} - 48^{\circ} = 42^{\circ}$ (angle sum of triangle).

subparts.text: $\angle BCE$.
subparts.label: iii
subparts.solution:
In isosceles $\triangle OAB$ ($OA = OB$, radii): $\angle OAB = \angle OBA = \dfrac{180^{\circ} - 50^{\circ}}{2} = 65^{\circ}$.
$\angle EAB = \angle OAB + \angle DAE = 65^{\circ} + 42^{\circ} = 107^{\circ}$.
$\angle BCE + \angle EAB = 180^{\circ}$ (angles in opposite segment of cyclic quadrilateral).
$\angle BCE = 180^{\circ} - 107^{\circ} = 73^{\circ}$.

parts.text: A semicircle $OHIJKL$, centre $O$, has radius 4.5 cm. The length of chord $IK$ is 6 cm.
parts.label: b

subparts.text: Show that angle $IOK = 1.46$ radians, correct to 3 significant figures.
subparts.label: i
subparts.answer: Using the cosine rule in $\triangle IOK$: $6^{2} = 4.5^{2} + 4.5^{2} - 2(4.5)(4.5)\cos\angle IOK$, so $\cos\angle IOK = \dfrac{40.5 - 36}{40.5} = \dfrac{1}{9}$, giving $\angle IOK = 1.4595\ldots \approx 1.46$ rad. Shown.
subparts.solution:
$M$ is the midpoint of $IK$, so $IM = KM = 3$ cm (perpendicular from centre bisects chord).
In right-angled $\triangle IOM$ with $OI = 4.5$, $IM = 3$:
$\sin\left(\dfrac{\angle IOK}{2}\right) = \dfrac{3}{4.5} = \dfrac{2}{3}$
$\dfrac{\angle IOK}{2} = 0.7297\ldots$
$\angle IOK = 1.4595\ldots \approx 1.46$ rad (3 s.f.). Shown.

subparts.text: Find the area of the shaded region.
subparts.label: ii
subparts.solution:
$\angle IOM = \dfrac{1.4595}{2} = 0.7297$ rad.
Area of sector $OIJ$ (where $J$ is at the top, with $OJ \perp IK$): use $\theta = 0.7297$ rad.
Area of sector $= \dfrac{1}{2}(4.5)^{2}(0.7297) \approx 7.388$ cm$^{2}$.
Area of $\triangle IOM = \dfrac{1}{2}(4.5)(4.5)\sin(0.7297) \approx 5.031$ cm$^{2}$ (or $\dfrac{1}{2}(3)(\sqrt{11.25})$).
Shaded area $= 7.388 - 5.031 = 2.357 \approx 2.36$ cm$^{2}$.

stem: The cumulative frequency curve shows the weekly expenditure on home deliveries of $160$ households from Block $W$.

parts.text: Use the cumulative frequency curve to find
parts.label: a

subparts.text: the median of the distribution,
subparts.label: i
subparts.solution:
From the cumulative frequency curve, the median is read at the $\frac{160}{2} = 80$th value.
Median $= \$44$

subparts.text: the interquartile range of the distribution,
subparts.label: ii
subparts.solution:
Lower quartile $Q_{1}$ (40th value) and upper quartile $Q_{3}$ (120th value) are read from the curve.
Interquartile range $= Q_{3} - Q_{1} = \$42$

subparts.text: the value of $p$, given that $p\%$ of the residents spent more than $\$84$ weekly on home deliveries.
subparts.label: iii
subparts.solution:
From the curve, the number of households spending more than $\$84$ is read off.
$p\% = \frac{\text{number spending more than } \$84}{160} \times 100\%$
$p = 7.5$

parts.text: The weekly expenditure on home deliveries of a group of $160$ residents from Block $K$ is displayed in the box-and-whisker plot below. Two statements compare the weekly expenditure on home deliveries of the residents from Block $W$ and Block $K$. For each statement, state whether you agree or disagree, giving a reason and stating clearly which statistic you used to make your decision.
parts.label: b

subparts.text: On average, the residents in Block $W$ have lower weekly expenses on home deliveries than the residents in Block $K$.
subparts.label: i
subparts.answer: Disagree. Block $W$ has a higher median expenditure of $\$44$ than Block $K$ ($\$34$).
subparts.solution: Disagree. The median weekly expenditure of Block $W$ ($\$44$) is higher than that of Block $K$ ($\$34$). Using the median, Block $W$ residents spend more on average, not less.

subparts.text: The weekly expenditure on home deliveries of the residents in Block $K$ is closer to the median than the weekly expenditure on home deliveries of the residents from Block $W$.
subparts.label: ii
subparts.answer: Agree. The interquartile range of Block $K$ ($\$36$) is lower than that of Block $W$ ($\$42$), so the data for Block $K$ is less widely spread.
subparts.solution: Agree. The interquartile range of Block $K$ ($\$36$) is smaller than that of Block $W$ ($\$42$). A smaller interquartile range means the data for Block $K$ is less spread out, i.e. closer to its median.

stem: $$y = -2x \qquad y = -2x+1$$ $$y = 2^x \qquad y = x^2$$ $$y = \dfrac{1}{x^2} \qquad y = \dfrac{1}{x}$$ Sketches of the graphs of some of these equations are drawn below. Write the correct equation beside each sketch.
The diagram shows a chocolate in the shape of a triangular prism.

parts.text: Calculate the volume of the chocolate.
parts.label: a
parts.solution:
The cross-section is a triangle with base $6$ cm and perpendicular height $5$ cm.
Area of cross-section $= \frac{1}{2} \times 6 \times 5 = 15$ cm$^2$
Volume $= 15 \times 15 = 225$ cm$^3$

parts.text: This chocolate is then melted and made into four pieces of spherical chocolate. Show that the radius of the spherical chocolate is 2.38 cm, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.label: b

parts.text: The diagram below shows a plane view of a box holding four of the spherical chocolates. The box is in the shape of a cuboid and the chocolates just fit into the box. Calculate the volume of empty space in the box.
parts.label: c
parts.solution:
The chocolates just fit, so the width and the height of the box are each one diameter and the length is four diameters.
Diameter $= 2 \times 2.38 = 4.76$ cm
Volume of box $= (4 \times 4.76) \times 4.76 \times 4.76 = 19.04 \times 4.76 \times 4.76 = 431.40$ cm$^3$
The four spheres were made from the melted prism, so their total volume is $225$ cm$^3$.
Volume of empty space $= 431.40 - 225 = 206.40 \approx 206$ cm$^3$ (3 s.f.)
(Using the unrounded $r = 2.378925$ gives $430.80 - 225 = 205.80$, which also rounds to $206$ cm$^3$.)

stem: 100 students from Group $A$ sat for a Mathematics test and their marks were recorded. The cumulative frequency curve shows the distribution of their marks.

parts.text: Use the curve to estimate
parts.label: a

subparts.text: the median,
subparts.label: i
subparts.solution: Median is at the $50$th student. Read across from cumulative frequency $50$ to the curve, then down to the $x$-axis: median $\approx 22$ marks.

subparts.text: the interquartile range.
subparts.label: ii
subparts.solution:
$Q_{1}$ at $25$th student $\approx 17$ marks; $Q_{3}$ at $75$th student $\approx 27$ marks.
$IQR = Q_{3} - Q_{1} \approx 27 - 17 = 10$ marks.

parts.text: Students who scored at most 15 marks must attend remedial classes. Estimate the number of students who need not attend remedial classes.
parts.label: b
parts.solution: Number scoring $\le 15$ marks (read from curve) $\approx 22$. So number who need NOT attend $= 100 - 22 = 78$ students.

parts.text: Last year, a group of 100 students sat for a similar Mathematics test and 45 of them scored more than 25 marks. Find the percentage change in the number of students who scored more than 25 marks for this year as compared to last year.
parts.label: c
parts.solution:
This year, number with $> 25$ marks $\approx 100 - 70 = 30$ (reading curve at $x = 25$ gives $\approx 70$). Last year $= 45$.
Percentage change $= \dfrac{30 - 45}{45} \times 100\% \approx -33.3\%$ (a decrease of $33.3\%$).

parts.text: 100 students from Group $B$ took the same Mathematics test. Their result is represented by the box-and-whisker plot shown. Make two comparisons between the performance of the students in these two groups.
parts.label: d
parts.answer: (1) Students from Group B performed better on average, with a higher median (28 vs 22). (2) Students from Group A had more consistent results, with a smaller IQR (10 vs 20 for Group B).
parts.solution:
Comparison 1: Group $B$ performed better on average — median for $B$ ($\approx 28$) is higher than for $A$ ($\approx 22$).
Comparison 2: Group $A$ was more consistent — $A$'s IQR ($\approx 10$) is smaller than $B$'s IQR ($\approx 20$), so $A$'s scores are less spread out.

stem: The heights of $200$ students in Sunflower Secondary School were recorded and a cumulative frequency curve was drawn.

parts.text: Use your graph to estimate
parts.label: a

subparts.text: the median height,
subparts.label: i

subparts.text: the interquartile range,
subparts.label: ii

subparts.label: iii

parts.label: b

subparts.label: i

subparts.label: ii

parts.text: The mass of the $200$ students were also recorded. All students whose mass were above $65$ kg underwent the school fitness programme for a period of $3$ months. After the programme, their mass were taken again and the box-and-whisker plots of their mass before and after the fitness programme were drawn.
parts.label: c

subparts.label: i
subparts.answer: Agree. Two reasons: (1) the median mass after the programme is lower than the median mass before the programme, indicating that on the whole students became lighter; (2) both the upper and lower quartiles of mass after are less than those before, and the maximum mass also decreased, showing a general reduction in mass across the group.

The point $E$ on the floor is such that $OE$ is perpendicular to the floor, as shown in the diagram.

The semi-vertical angle of the lampshade is $\frac{\pi}{3}$. Winnie and his three friends each sits at one of the four corners $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$ to read. parts.text: The diagram shows the sketch of $y = ax^2 + 4x + 5$, where $a$ is an integer. State a possible value for $a$.

stem:
The wooden table in a cafe is as seen in the diagram. It consists of two solid parts: a circular table top with thickness $2.5$ cm and diameter $90$ cm, and a cylindrical bottom with height $40$ cm and diameter $35$ cm.
The table shows the cost required to paint the wooden tables in the cafe.
$$\begin{array}{|l|c|c|c|} \hline \text{Paint type} & \text{Area Coverage (cm}^2\text{ per litre)} & \text{Cost (\$ per litre)} & \text{Labour Cost (\$ per table)} \\ \hline \text{Primer Single Coat} & 5000 & 12 & 4 \\ \hline \text{Double Coat Paint} & 3000 & 28 & 8 \\ \hline \end{array}$$

parts.text: Show that the total surface area of a wooden table to be painted is approximately $16900$ cm$^2$.
parts.label: a
parts.solution:
The table top has radius $45$ cm and thickness $2.5$ cm; the cylinder has radius $17.5$ cm and height $40$ cm.
Top face of the table top $= \pi (45)^2 = 6361.725$ cm$^2$
Curved face of the table top $= 2\pi (45)(2.5) = 706.858$ cm$^2$
Curved face of the cylinder $= 2\pi (17.5)(40) = 4398.229$ cm$^2$
Underside of the table top (a ring) $= \pi (45)^2 - \pi (17.5)^2 = 6361.725 - 962.112 = 5399.612$ cm$^2$
Total surface area $= 6361.725 + 706.858 + 4398.229 + 5399.612 = 16866.4$ cm$^2 \approx 16900$ cm$^2$ (shown)

parts.text: Benny has set aside a budget of $\$3000$ for the paint job. Assuming primer single coat paint is used for the cylindrical bottom and double coat paint is used for the circular top, what is the maximum number of tables that can be painted in the cafe?
parts.label: b
parts.solution:
Circular top (double coat paint): area $= 6361.725 + 706.858 + 5399.612 = 12468.195$ cm$^2$
Paint needed $= \dfrac{12468.195}{3000} = 4.156$ litres, costing $4.156 \times \$28 = \$116.37$
Labour for the top $= \$8$
Cylindrical bottom (primer single coat): area $= 4398.229$ cm$^2$
Paint needed $= \dfrac{4398.229}{5000} = 0.87965$ litres, costing $0.87965 \times \$12 = \$10.56$
Labour for the bottom $= \$4$
Total cost per table $= \$116.37 + \$8 + \$10.56 + \$4 = \$138.92$
Number of tables $= \dfrac{3000}{138.92} = 21.59...$
Maximum number of tables that can be painted $= 21$

stem: The line graphs below show the performance of Jack and Ben in the school Mathematics assessment for the first semester. Upon observing these line graphs, a classmate commented that Ben has made better improvement than Jack. Do you agree? Justify your answer.

[Volume of cone $V = \dfrac{1}{3}\pi r^{2}h$; Curved surface area of cone $= \pi r l$] A toy manufacturer uses thin acrylic sheets to make a hollow cone of radius $r$ cm, height $h$ cm and slanted height $l$ cm as shown in Fig. 1. The hollow cone holds $200 \text{ cm}^{3}$ of water when completely filled. It is given that the external curved surface area of the cone is $S$.

parts.text: Use differentiation to find the value of $r$ which gives the minimum value of $S$.
parts.label: b
parts.solution:
$S^2 = \pi^2 r^4 + \dfrac{360000}{r^2}$
Differentiate w.r.t. $r$:
$2S\dfrac{dS}{dr} = 4\pi^2 r^3 - \dfrac{720000}{r^3}$
When $\dfrac{dS}{dr} = 0$:
$4\pi^2 r^3 - \dfrac{720000}{r^3} = 0$
$\pi^2 r^6 - 180000 = 0$
$r = \sqrt[6]{\dfrac{180000}{\pi^2}} \approx 5.1305 \approx 5.13$
By the 2nd derivative test:
$2\left(\dfrac{dS}{dr}\right)^2 + 2S\dfrac{d^2S}{dr^2} = 12\pi^2 r^2 + \dfrac{2160000}{r^4}$
When $\dfrac{dS}{dr} = 0$, $r = 5.1305$ and $S = 143.23$:
$\dfrac{d^2S}{dr^2} = \dfrac{1}{2S}\left(12\pi^2 r^2 + \dfrac{2160000}{r^4}\right) = 21.766 > 0$
Hence $S$ is minimum when $r = 5.13$.

parts.text: Show that $r = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}h$ when $S$ is a minimum.
parts.label: c
parts.solution:
When $r = \sqrt[6]{\dfrac{180000}{\pi^2}}$ and $h = \dfrac{600}{\pi r^2}$:
$\dfrac{r}{h} = \dfrac{r}{\dfrac{600}{\pi r^2}} = \dfrac{\pi r^3}{600} = \dfrac{\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{180000}{\pi^2}}}{600} = \dfrac{300\sqrt{2}}{600} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$
$\therefore r = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}h$

parts.text: The manufacturer makes two of the hollow cones with dimensions found in parts (b) and (c). The two cones are positioned above each other with a common vertical axis, as shown in Fig. 2. The lower cone is completely filled with water and water spills from the lower cone as the upper cone is lowered vertically at a constant rate of $\dfrac{dp}{dt} = 0.5$, where $p$ cm is the distance the upper cone has descended into the water after $t$ seconds. The volume of water remaining in the lower cone at time $t$ is $V \text{ cm}^{3}$. It is given that $p = 0$ when $t = 0$. Find the rate of change of $V$ when $p = 2$.
parts.label: d
parts.solution:
$V = 200 - \dfrac{1}{3}\pi r_p^2 p$, where $r_p = \dfrac{p}{\sqrt{2}}$ by (iii):
$= 200 - \dfrac{1}{3}\pi\left(\dfrac{p}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2 p$
$V = 200 - \dfrac{1}{6}\pi p^3$
$\dfrac{dV}{dp} = -\dfrac{1}{2}\pi p^2$
When $p = 2$:
$\dfrac{dV}{dt} = \dfrac{dV}{dp} \times \dfrac{dp}{dt} = -\dfrac{1}{2}\pi(2)^2 \times 0.5 = -\pi$
Rate of change of $V$ is $-\pi \text{ cm}^3\text{s}^{-1}$.

stem: In Australia, concrete bollards in the shape of frustums are used as barricades on the roads. Singapore government intends to construct concrete bollards similar to the ones in Australia. The frustum is obtained by removing a right circular cone by a plane parallel to the base of the original cone. The shape of each bollard is modelled below, where the frustum has base radius 10 cm, top radius 4 cm and height 30 cm, and the original cone has base radius 10 cm and height 50 cm.

parts.text: Show that the volume of the frustum is 0.00490 m$^3$, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.label: a

stem: The picture shows a concrete sculpture in Rotterdam, Netherlands, made of three identical square slabs of side $8$ m. The three slabs are assembled perpendicular to each other such that they meet at one common point $O$. Each slab has one vertex fixed to the flat horizontal ground, represented by the plane $\pi$, and one vertex fixed to the centre of another slab. The slab $p_A$ is part of the plane $x = 0$. It has one vertex, point $A$, on $\pi$ and another vertex on the centre of $p_C$. The slab $p_B$ is part of the plane $y = 0$. It has one vertex, point $B$, on $\pi$ and another vertex on the centre of $p_A$. The remaining two vertices are denoted as $D$ and $E$. The slab $p_C$ is part of the plane $z = 0$. It has one vertex, point $C$, on $\pi$ and another vertex on the centre of $p_B$. The point $O$ is taken as the origin and perpendicular unit vectors $\mathbf{i}, \mathbf{j}$ and $\mathbf{k}$ are defined, as shown in the diagram, with $\mathbf{i}, \mathbf{j}, \mathbf{k}$ along one edge of $p_C, p_A, p_B$ respectively. For example, point $D$ has position vector $8\mathbf{i} + 4\mathbf{k}$. It is assumed that the slabs are made of materials with negligible thickness.

parts.text: Show that a Cartesian equation of $\pi$ is $x + y - z = 12$.
parts.label: i
parts.solution:
$\overrightarrow{OA} = \begin{pmatrix}0\\4\\-8\end{pmatrix},\ \overrightarrow{OB} = \begin{pmatrix}8\\0\\-4\end{pmatrix},\ \overrightarrow{OC} = \begin{pmatrix}4\\8\\0\end{pmatrix}$
$\overrightarrow{AB} = \begin{pmatrix}8\\-4\\4\end{pmatrix} = 4\begin{pmatrix}2\\-1\\1\end{pmatrix},\quad \overrightarrow{AC} = \begin{pmatrix}4\\4\\8\end{pmatrix} = 4\begin{pmatrix}1\\1\\2\end{pmatrix}$
Normal of plane $\pi = \begin{pmatrix}2\\-1\\1\end{pmatrix}\times\begin{pmatrix}1\\1\\2\end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix}-3\\-3\\3\end{pmatrix} = -3\begin{pmatrix}1\\1\\-1\end{pmatrix}$
Equation of $\pi$: $\mathbf{r}\cdot\begin{pmatrix}1\\1\\-1\end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix}0\\4\\-8\end{pmatrix}\cdot\begin{pmatrix}1\\1\\-1\end{pmatrix} = 12$
$x + y - z = 12$.

parts.text: To make the sculpture more stable, plans are made to construct a vertical support from $O$ to a point $F$ on $\pi$, such that $OF$ is perpendicular to $\pi$. Find the position vector of $F$.
parts.label: ii
parts.solution:
Equation of line $OF$: $\mathbf{r} = \lambda\begin{pmatrix}1\\1\\-1\end{pmatrix}$
For the coordinates of $F$: $\lambda\begin{pmatrix}1\\1\\-1\end{pmatrix}\cdot\begin{pmatrix}1\\1\\-1\end{pmatrix} = 12 \Rightarrow 3\lambda = 12 \Rightarrow \lambda = 4$.
$\overrightarrow{OF} = 4\begin{pmatrix}1\\1\\-1\end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix}4\\4\\-4\end{pmatrix}$
Coordinates of $F$ are $(4,4,-4)$.

parts.text: A pigeon is at a point $P(2,11,1)$. It flies in a straight line and rests on the sculpture along the edge $DE$. Given that the pigeon rests at the point nearest to $P$, find the coordinates of this point. Hence find the distance the pigeon flew.
parts.label: iii
parts.solution:
Equation of line $DE$: $\mathbf{r} = \begin{pmatrix}8\\0\\4\end{pmatrix} + t\begin{pmatrix}1\\0\\0\end{pmatrix}$
Let the point on $DE$ nearest to $P$ be $Q$ with position vector $\begin{pmatrix}8+\lambda\\0\\4\end{pmatrix}$.
$\left(\begin{pmatrix}8+\lambda\\0\\4\end{pmatrix} - \begin{pmatrix}2\\11\\1\end{pmatrix}\right)\cdot\begin{pmatrix}1\\0\\0\end{pmatrix} = 0$
$6 + \lambda = 0 \Rightarrow \lambda = -6$
Hence $\overrightarrow{OQ} = \begin{pmatrix}2\\0\\4\end{pmatrix}$, i.e. the point nearest to $P$ is $(2,0,4)$.
Shortest distance $= PQ = \left|\begin{pmatrix}2\\0\\4\end{pmatrix} - \begin{pmatrix}2\\11\\1\end{pmatrix}\right| = \left|\begin{pmatrix}0\\-11\\3\end{pmatrix}\right| = \sqrt{130}\text{ m}$.

parts.text: Another pigeon has flight path with equation $\dfrac{x-1}{3} = \dfrac{2-y}{4} = z+3$. Without using a calculator, determine if the flight paths of the two pigeons cross.
parts.label: iv
parts.answer: No, the flight paths do not cross.
parts.solution:
$\dfrac{x-1}{3} = \dfrac{2-y}{4} = z+3 \Rightarrow \mathbf{r} = \begin{pmatrix}1\\2\\-3\end{pmatrix} + \mu\begin{pmatrix}3\\-4\\1\end{pmatrix}$
First pigeon's path: $\mathbf{r} = \begin{pmatrix}2\\0\\4\end{pmatrix} + \lambda\begin{pmatrix}0\\-11\\3\end{pmatrix}$
Equating the two flight paths:
$\begin{pmatrix}1+3\mu\\2-4\mu\\-3+\mu\end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix}2\\-11\lambda\\4+3\lambda\end{pmatrix}$
Solving the first two equations: $\mu = \dfrac{1}{3}$ and $\lambda = -\dfrac{2}{33}$.
Substituting into the third equation: $-3 + \dfrac{1}{3} = -\dfrac{8}{3} \neq \dfrac{42}{11} = 4 - \dfrac{2}{11}$.
Thus, the flight paths do not cross.

stem: [It is given that the curved surface area and volume of a right circular cone with radius $r$, slant height $l$ and height $h$ are $\pi r l$ and $\frac{1}{3}\pi r^{2}h$ respectively.] A workshop makes a closed right circular cone clay sculpture with radius $r$ cm, slant height $l$ cm, height $h$ cm and a semi-vertical angle of $\frac{\pi}{6}$ radians, as shown in Figure 1.

parts.text: Assume the closed conical clay sculpture is uniformly expanding when heated (its shape is unchanged, so $\frac{r}{h}$ remains constant). Show that the height of the sculpture is $14$ cm at the instant when the ratio of the rate of increase of the total surface area to the rate of increase of its volume is $3:7$.
parts.label: a
parts.solution:
Semi-vertical angle $\frac{\pi}{6}$: $r=h\tan\frac{\pi}{6}=\frac{h}{\sqrt{3}}$, $l=\frac{h}{\cos\frac{\pi}{6}}=\frac{2h}{\sqrt{3}}$.
Total surface area $S=\pi r^2+\pi r l=\pi r(r+l)=\pi\cdot\frac{h}{\sqrt{3}}\cdot\sqrt{3}\,h=\pi h^2$.
Volume $V=\frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h=\frac{\pi h^3}{9}$.
$\frac{dS}{dt}=2\pi h\frac{dh}{dt}$, $\frac{dV}{dt}=\frac{\pi h^2}{3}\frac{dh}{dt}$.
$\frac{dS/dt}{dV/dt}=\frac{2\pi h}{\pi h^2/3}=\frac{6}{h}=\frac{3}{7}\Rightarrow h=14$. (Shown)

parts.text: A total of 15 such identical sculptures, each of height 14 cm, are stacked vertically to make a static display (Figure 2). The display is placed on top of a museum of height $8.6$ m. A passer-by's eye level is $1.5$ m above ground, and the display subtends an angle of $\theta$ radians at the eye level (Figure 3).
parts.label: b

subparts.text: Show that $\tan\theta = \dfrac{2.1x}{x^{2} + 65.32}$, where $x$ m is the horizontal distance from the base of the museum to the passer-by.
subparts.label: i
subparts.solution:
Display height $=15\times14\text{ cm}=2.1$ m.
Heights above eye level: top $=8.6+2.1-1.5=9.2$ m, bottom $=8.6-1.5=7.1$ m.
$\tan\theta=\frac{9.2/x-7.1/x}{1+\frac{(9.2)(7.1)}{x^2}}=\frac{2.1/x}{\frac{x^2+65.32}{x^2}}=\frac{2.1x}{x^2+65.32}$. (Shown)

subparts.text: The optimal angle $\theta$ is where $\tan\theta$ is maximised. Determine, by differentiation, the distance from the base of the museum at which the passer-by should stand to subtend the optimal angle.
subparts.label: ii
subparts.solution:
$\frac{d}{dx}\left(\frac{2.1x}{x^2+65.32}\right)=\frac{2.1(65.32-x^2)}{(x^2+65.32)^2}$.
Setting this to $0$: $x^2=65.32$.
$x=\sqrt{65.32}\approx 8.08$ m (taking the positive value).

stem:
Karen is selling pancakes for a one-day charity event. She specialises in three different types of pancakes which are plain, chocolate and cheese at the cost of $\$2$, $\$3$ and $\$4$ each respectively. The matrix $\mathbf{A}$ shows the average number of pancakes sold in the morning and afternoon of the day. The necessary ingredients for the pancake recipe are shown in the second diagram. The price for each ingredient is as follows:
$$\begin{array}{|l|l|l|l|} \hline \text{Ingredient} & \text{Packaging} & \text{Unit Price} & \text{Bundle price} \\ \hline \text{Eggs} & \text{1 tray of 30} & \$6 & - \\ \hline \text{Milk} & \text{1 litre carton} & \$3.50 & \text{Buy 2 for }\$5.95 \\ \hline \text{Self-raising flour} & \text{1 kg packet} & \$2.50 & - \\ \hline \text{Cocoa powder} & \text{1 kg tin} & \$13.50 & - \\ \hline \text{Cream cheese} & \text{1 kg block} & \$15.50 & - \\ \hline \end{array}$$

subparts.text: Evaluate the matrix $\mathbf{T} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 \end{pmatrix} \mathbf{A}$.
subparts.label: i
subparts.solution:
$\mathbf{T} = (1\ \ 1)\,\mathbf{A}$ adds the morning and afternoon rows of $\mathbf{A}$:
$= (83 + 46\ \ \ \ \ 86 + 67\ \ \ \ \ 72 + 47)$
$= (129\ \ \ \ \ 153\ \ \ \ \ 119)$

subparts.text: State what each element of matrix $\mathbf{T}$ represents.
subparts.label: ii
subparts.answer: Each element represents the total number of plain, chocolate and cheese pancakes sold that day, respectively.
subparts.solution: Each element of $\mathbf{T}$ represents the total number of pancakes of that type (plain, chocolate and cheese respectively) sold for the whole day.

subparts.text: Using matrix multiplication, find the total revenue from the sales.
subparts.label: iii

parts.text: Given that all profit earned from this charity event will be donated to the Voluntary Welfare Organisation, is it true that her donation is more than $900\%$ of her cost price? Justify your answer and show all your workings clearly.
parts.label: b
parts.answer: Not true. Cost price $\approx \$120.73$ and profit $\approx \$1072.27$, giving a ratio of about $889\%$, which is less than $900\%$.
parts.solution:
Total pancakes: plain $129$, chocolate $153$, cheese $119$ (total $401$).
Number of basic batches ($12$ pancakes each) $= \lceil \frac{401}{12} \rceil = 34$ batches, requiring:
Eggs: $34 \times 2 = 68 \Rightarrow 3$ trays $= 3 \times \$6 = \$18$
Milk: $34 \times 500 = 17\,000$ ml $= 17$ L $\Rightarrow 8$ bundles $+ 1$ carton $= 8(\$5.95) + \$3.50 = \$51.10$
Flour: $34 \times 255 = 8670$ g $\Rightarrow 9$ kg $= 9 \times \$2.50 = \$22.50$
Cocoa (chocolate): $\lceil\frac{153}{12}\rceil \times 60 = 780$ g $\Rightarrow 1$ kg $= \$13.50$
Cream cheese (cheese): $\lceil\frac{119}{12}\rceil \times 100 = 1000$ g $= 1$ kg $= \$15.50$
Total cost $= 18 + 51.10 + 22.50 + 13.50 + 15.50 = \$120.60$
Profit $= 1193 - 120.60 = \$1072.40$
$\frac{\text{profit}}{\text{cost}} = \frac{1072.40}{120.60} \times 100\% \approx 889\%$
Since $889\% < 900\%$, the statement is not true.

stem: Figure 1 shows a scented candle in the shape of a right circular cone with a diameter of 30 cm and a slant height of 17 cm.

parts.text: Find the volume of the candle. Leave your answer correct to the nearest cubic centimetre.
parts.label: a
parts.solution:
Cone: diameter $= 30$ cm, so radius $r = 15$ cm; slant height $l = 17$ cm.
Vertical height $h = \sqrt{l^2 - r^2} = \sqrt{17^2 - 15^2} = \sqrt{64} = 8$ cm.
Volume $= \dfrac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h = \dfrac{1}{3}\pi (15)^2 (8) = 600\pi = 1884.96\ldots \approx 1885$ cm$^3$

parts.text: The candle is lit from the top and melted at a constant rate. It will take 10 hours for it to be fully melted. Figure 2 shows the remaining candle in the shape of a frustum after being lit for 1 hour 15 minutes. Find the ratio of the melted volume to the original volume of the candle.
parts.label: b
parts.solution:
Time lit $= 1$ h $15$ min $= 1.25$ h, out of $10$ h total.
Fraction melted $= \dfrac{1.25}{10} = \dfrac{1}{8}$.
Ratio of melted volume to original volume $= 1 : 8$

parts.text: Find the area of the shaded region in Figure 2.
parts.label: c
parts.solution:
Since the cone melts uniformly, the melted-off top cone is similar to the original.
Volume scale factor $= \dfrac{1}{8}$, so linear scale factor $= \sqrt[3]{\dfrac{1}{8}} = \dfrac{1}{2}$.
Top cone: $r_{\text{top}} = 7.5$ cm, $l_{\text{top}} = 8.5$ cm.
Curved surface area of frustum (shaded) $= \pi R l - \pi r l_{\text{top}} = \pi(15)(17) - \pi(7.5)(8.5)$
$= 255\pi - 63.75\pi = 191.25\pi \approx 600.88$
Plus top circle of radius $7.5$: $\pi(7.5)^2 = 56.25\pi$.
Total shaded area $\approx 177$ cm$^2$ (based on shaded region as indicated in Figure 2).

parts.text: The remaining candle is placed in a container with the same base area and height of the remaining candle as shown in Figure 3. Calculate the volume of empty space not occupied by the remaining candle in Figure 3.
parts.label: d
parts.solution:
Remaining candle (frustum) volume $= \dfrac{7}{8} \times 1885 \approx 1649.3$ cm$^3$.
Container is a cylinder with base radius $= 15$ cm (same as candle base) and height $= $ height of remaining frustum $= 7$ cm.
Cylinder volume $= \pi (15)^2 (7) = 1575\pi \approx 4948$ cm$^3$.
Empty space $= 4948 - 1649 \approx 1180$ cm$^3$ (to 4 s.f.: $1178$ cm$^3$)

stem: The diagram below shows the top view of a cylindrical box containing four spherical candles. $O$ is the centre of the box. $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$ are the centres of the candles. The radius of each candle is $3$ cm.

parts.text: Calculate the volume of one spherical candle.
parts.label: a
parts.solution:
Volume of $1$ candle $= \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^{3}$
$\phantom{\text{Volume}} = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi (3)^{3}$
$\phantom{\text{Volume}} = 113.10$
$\phantom{\text{Volume}} \approx 113$ cm$^{3}$ (3 s.f.)

parts.text: Show that the radius of the box is $7.243$ cm, corrected to three decimal places.
parts.label: b
parts.answer: Shown: $OA = \sqrt{3^{2} + 3^{2}} = 3\sqrt{2}$ cm, so radius of box $= 3\sqrt{2} + 3 = 7.2426\ldots \approx 7.243$ cm.
parts.solution:
Diagonal from centre of box to centre of corner candle:
$OA = \sqrt{3^{2} + 3^{2}} = 3\sqrt{2}$ cm
Radius of box $= OA + 3$
$\phantom{\text{Radius}} = 3\sqrt{2} + 3$
$\phantom{\text{Radius}} = 7.2426\ldots$
$\phantom{\text{Radius}} \approx 7.243$ cm (3 d.p.) (shown)

parts.text: The four spherical candles are melted and recast into one large candle as shown below. The candle is of the shape of a square pyramid. The height of the pyramid is $1.5$ times the length of the square base. Find the height, $h$, of the pyramid.
parts.label: c
parts.solution:
Let the length of the square base be $s$. Then $h = 1.5s$.
Total volume of $4$ candles $= 4 \times 113.097 = 452.39$ cm$^{3}$
Volume of pyramid $= \dfrac{1}{3} \times s^{2} \times h$
$\dfrac{1}{3} \times s^{2} \times 1.5s = 452.39$
$0.5 s^{3} = 452.39$
$s^{3} = 904.78$
$s = 9.668$ cm
$h = 1.5 \times 9.668$
$\phantom{h} = 14.5$ cm (3 s.f.)

stem: [A cone of radius $r$ and height $h$ has volume $V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h$.]

parts.text: An ornament consists of a sphere of fixed radius $r$ cm inscribed in a right circular cone. The sphere is in contact with the base of the cone at the point $P$, and with the inner surfaces of the cone at the points $D$ and $E$ respectively, as shown in the diagram. Each of the lengths $AB$ and $AC$ makes an angle of $\theta$ radians with the downward vertical.
parts.label: a

subparts.text: Show that the volume of the cone, $V$ cm$^3$, is given by $V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^3 (1 + \csc\theta)^3 \tan^2\theta$.
subparts.label: i
subparts.solution:
$V = \frac{1}{3}\pi(PC)^2(AP)$
In $\triangle AOE$, $\sin\theta = \frac{r}{AO} \Rightarrow AO = r\csc\theta$.
$\therefore AP = r + r\csc\theta = r(1 + \csc\theta)$
In $\triangle APC$, $\tan\theta = \frac{PC}{AP} \Rightarrow PC = AP\tan\theta = r(1 + \csc\theta)\tan\theta$
$V = \frac{1}{3}\pi[r(1 + \csc\theta)\tan\theta]^2 \cdot r(1 + \csc\theta)$
$V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^3(1 + \csc\theta)^3\tan^2\theta$ (shown)

subparts.text: Using differentiation, show that the volume of the cone is minimum when $\sin\theta = \frac{1}{3}$.
subparts.label: ii
subparts.solution:
$\frac{dV}{d\theta} = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^3\left[3(1 + \csc\theta)^2(-\csc\theta\cot\theta)\tan^2\theta + (1 + \csc\theta)^3 \cdot 2\tan\theta\sec^2\theta\right]$
$= \frac{1}{3}\pi r^3(1 + \csc\theta)^2\left[-3\csc\theta\tan\theta + 2(1 + \csc\theta)\tan\theta\sec^2\theta\right]$
Setting $\frac{dV}{d\theta} = 0$:
$(1 + \csc\theta)^2 = 0 \Rightarrow \csc\theta = -1 \Rightarrow \sin\theta = -1$ (N.A.)
or $-\frac{3}{\cos\theta} + \frac{\sin\theta + 1}{\sin\theta} \cdot \frac{2\sin\theta}{\cos^3\theta} = 0$
$-\frac{3}{\cos\theta} + \frac{2(\sin\theta + 1)}{\cos^3\theta} = 0$
$-3\cos^2\theta + 2\sin\theta + 2 = 0$
$-3(1 - \sin^2\theta) + 2\sin\theta + 2 = 0$
$3\sin^2\theta + 2\sin\theta - 1 = 0$
$(\sin\theta + 1)(3\sin\theta - 1) = 0$
$\sin\theta = -1$ (N.A.) or $\sin\theta = \frac{1}{3}$
When $\sin\theta = \frac{1}{3}$, from G.C., $\frac{d^2V}{d\theta^2} = 75.4r^3 > 0$ since $r > 0$.
$\therefore V$ is minimum when $\sin\theta = \frac{1}{3}$.

parts.text: Another ornament in the shape of an hour-glass is made up of two identical right circular cones of fixed height $H$ cm and slant height $\sqrt{6}H$ cm as shown in the diagram below. The hour-glass is filled with some luminous liquid such that when inverted, the liquid in the upper cone flows into the lower cone at a rate of $4$ cm$^3$ s$^{-1}$ through a hole of negligible size at $K$. At time $t$ s, the depth of the liquid in the lower cone is $h$ cm.
parts.label: b

subparts.text: Show that $W$ cm$^3$, the volume of liquid in the lower cone at time $t$ s, is given by $W = \frac{5}{3}\pi\left[ H^3 - (H - h)^3 \right]$.
subparts.label: i
subparts.solution:
Let $R$ be the radius of the cone and $x$ the radius of the water level when the depth of water is $h$ cm.
Radius of cone, $R = \sqrt{(\sqrt{6}H)^2 - H^2} = \sqrt{5}H$.
By similar triangles, $\frac{x}{R} = \frac{H - h}{H} \Rightarrow \frac{x}{\sqrt{5}H} = \frac{H - h}{H} \Rightarrow x = \sqrt{5}(H - h)$.
Volume of liquid in the lower cone at time $t$:
$W = \frac{1}{3}\pi R^2 H - \frac{1}{3}\pi x^2(H - h)$
$= \frac{1}{3}\pi(\sqrt{5}H)^2 H - \frac{1}{3}\pi(\sqrt{5}(H - h))^2(H - h)$
$= \frac{5}{3}\pi H^3 - \frac{5}{3}\pi(H - h)^3$ (shown)

subparts.text: Find the rate of increase of the depth of the liquid in the lower cone when the depth of the liquid in the lower cone is $\frac{1}{25}H$ cm. Leave your answer in exact form in terms of $\pi$ and $H$.
subparts.label: ii
subparts.solution:
$\frac{dW}{dh} = 5\pi(H - h)^2$. Given $\frac{dW}{dt} = 4$ cm$^3$ s$^{-1}$.
$\frac{dW}{dt} = \frac{dW}{dh} \times \frac{dh}{dt}$
$4 = 5\pi(H - h)^2 \times \frac{dh}{dt}$
When $h = \frac{1}{25}H$:
$4 = 5\pi\left(\frac{24}{25}H\right)^2 \times \frac{dh}{dt}$
$\frac{dh}{dt} = \frac{125}{144\pi H^2}$ cm s$^{-1}$

stem:
A chock is a block placed against a wheel or rounded object, to prevent it from moving. Jenny had to come up with a prototype for the design of a new wheel chock. Jenny drew a model of the wheel chock and the cross section is shown below.

In the diagram, the shaded region $ABC$ represents the cross section of the model of the wheel chock. $OAC$ is a sector of a circle with centre $O$ and radius $r\text{ cm}$. $AB = 14\text{ cm}$, $\angle AOC = x$ radians and $OC$ is perpendicular to $CB$.

parts.text: Show that $BC = \sqrt{28(7 + r)}$.
parts.label: a
parts.answer: $OB = OA + AB = r + 14$. By Pythagoras in $\triangle OCB$ (right-angled at $C$): $BC^{2} = OB^{2} - OC^{2} = (r+14)^{2} - r^{2} = 28r + 196 = 28(r + 7)$. Hence $BC = \sqrt{28(7+r)}$.
parts.solution:
$OB = OA + AB = r + 14$
$OC$ is a radius, so $OC = r$, and $OC \perp CB$.
By Pythagoras' theorem in right-angled $\triangle OCB$:
$BC^{2} = OB^{2} - OC^{2} = (r+14)^{2} - r^{2}$
$= r^{2} + 28r + 196 - r^{2} = 28r + 196$
$= 28(r + 7)$
$BC = \sqrt{28(7+r)}$ (shown)

parts.text: Find the area of the shaded region $ABC$, given that $BC = 20\text{ cm}$.
parts.label: b
parts.answer: $28(7+r) = 400 \Rightarrow r = \tfrac{51}{7}$. $\cos x = \tfrac{r}{r+14} = \tfrac{51}{149}$, so $x \approx 1.2217\text{ rad}$. Area of shaded region $= $ area of $\triangle OCB -$ area of sector $OAC = \tfrac{1}{2}(r)(20) - \tfrac{1}{2}r^{2}x \approx 72.86 - 32.43 \approx 40.4\text{ cm}^{2}$.
parts.solution:
$28(7+r) = 20^{2} = 400$
$7 + r = \dfrac{100}{7}$
$r = \dfrac{100}{7} - 7 = \dfrac{51}{7} \approx 7.286\text{ cm}$

In right-angled $\triangle OCB$: $\cos x = \dfrac{OC}{OB} = \dfrac{r}{r+14} = \dfrac{51/7}{149/7} = \dfrac{51}{149}$
$x = \cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{51}{149}\right) \approx 1.2217\text{ rad}$

Area of $\triangle OCB = \dfrac{1}{2}(OC)(CB) = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{51}{7}\right)(20) \approx 72.86\text{ cm}^{2}$
Area of sector $OAC = \dfrac{1}{2}r^{2}x = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{51}{7}\right)^{2}(1.2217) \approx 32.43\text{ cm}^{2}$
Shaded area $= 72.86 - 32.43 \approx 40.4\text{ cm}^{2}$ (3 s.f.)

parts.text: Jenny claimed that the points $O$, $B$ and $C$ lie on the circumference of the circle. Do you agree? Explain with reasons.
parts.label: c
parts.answer: Agree. Since $\angle OCB = 90°$, by the converse of Thales' theorem (angle in a semicircle), the three points $O$, $B$ and $C$ lie on a circle with $OB$ as diameter.
parts.solution:
Agree.
$\angle OCB = 90°$ (given that $OC$ is perpendicular to $CB$).
By the converse of the angle-in-a-semicircle theorem, if a point subtends a right angle at a segment, that point lies on the circle having the segment as diameter.
So $C$ lies on the circle with $OB$ as diameter, and $O$ and $B$ are endpoints of that diameter.
Hence $O$, $B$ and $C$ all lie on the circumference of that circle.

stem: Mr Graham bought a 2-room flat in Sembawang. The floor plan can be modelled as five rectangles as shown below.

parts.text: Calculate the total floor area of Mr Graham's kitchen.
parts.label: a

parts.text: The optimal kitchen cabinets' height, including the counter top, is calculated based on the concept of ergonomics. Using the diagram as reference, kitchen cabinet designers view that optimal cabinet height should be the distance between one's elbow and the ground, with 10 cm allowance for elbow movement. The diagram below shows a drawing of Mrs Graham whose height is 168 cm. Calculate the range of optimal kitchen cabinets' heights, including the counter top, for Mrs Graham.
parts.label: b
parts.solution:
10 cm represents 168 cm, so 1 cm represents 16.8 cm.
Elbow to ground $= 6.4$ cm
$6.4\times 16.8 = 107.52$ cm
Range of optimal kitchen cabinet heights $= 107.52-10 = 97.52$ cm to $107.52$ cm.

parts.text:
Mr Graham plans to install a combination of kitchen cabinets along the L-shaped shaded area in the kitchen. In the combination, he requires one of the cabinets to have a sink, a corner cabinet and at least one of the other cabinets to have wire basket shelves. He wants to customise the height of the cabinets to suit Mrs Graham's height. He also wishes to install a counter top for the top of the cabinet, considering to use either granite, ceramic or acrylic as its material. He has a budget of $\$2200$ to purchase the kitchen cabinets and L-shaped counter top. Using the given tables and your answer in (b), propose a possible combination that will best suit Mr Graham's requirements that will optimise storage and space while maximising the use of his budget.

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|} \hline \textbf{Cabinet} & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 5 & 6 \\ \hline \text{Description} & \text{sink, 1 drawer, 1 door} & \text{corner} & \text{4 drawers} & \text{2 shelves, 2 doors} & \text{1 door + wire basket} & \text{1 drawer, 3 shelves, 1 door} \\ \hline \text{Cost} & \$156 & \$166 & \$260 & \$290 & \$166 & \$193 \\ \hline \text{Width (cm)} & 50 & 60 & 90 & 80 & 60 & 70 \\ \hline \text{Depth (cm)} & 60 & 60 & 60 & 60 & 60 & 60 \\ \hline \end{array}$$
Height customisation: 50 cm free, up to 75 cm $\$15$, up to 105 cm $\$25$.
Counter top materials: Granite $\$1200$, Ceramic $\$800$, Acrylic $\$600$.
parts.label: c
parts.answer: Choose cabinets 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 (cabinets: $\$1231$) with height $\$25 \times 6=\$150$, plus Ceramic counter top $\$800$. Total $=\$2181$, leaving $\$19$ in budget.
parts.solution:
Compulsory: a sink cabinet, a corner cabinet and a wire-basket-shelf cabinet, i.e. Cabinet 1 + Cabinet 2 (at the junction of the wall) + Cabinet 5.
Remaining length $= 342-50-60-50 = 172$ cm; remaining width $= 135-60 = 75$ cm.
Current total cost $= \$156+\$166+\$166 = \$488$.
Along the length: 1 Cabinet 3 + 1 Cabinet 4 ($90$ cm $+ 80$ cm); along the width: 1 Cabinet 6 ($70$ cm), to optimise storage.
Total cost of cabinets $= \$488+\$193+\$260+\$290 = \$1231$.
Height customisation $= \$25\times 6 = \$150$.
Remaining budget $= \$2200-\$1231-\$150 = \$819$, so a Ceramic ($\$800$) or Acrylic ($\$600$) counter top is affordable.
Mr Graham should choose the Ceramic counter top with cabinets 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 (total $= \$2181$), leaving $\$19$ in his budget.

stem: [It is given that a right circular cone of radius $r$ and height $h$ has total surface area $\pi r^2 + \pi r\sqrt{r^2 + h^2}$ and volume $\frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h$.] An ice-cream company plans to launch a new product called Tasty Cone into the market. Each Tasty Cone is in the shape of a right circular cone with a base radius $r$ cm and height $h$ cm as shown in Fig. 1.

parts.text: The volume of each Tasty Cone is set by the company to be $100$ ml and the total surface area, $S$ cm$^2$, should be as small as possible to reduce the cost of packaging. It is given that $1$ ml $= 1$ cm$^3$. Show that $S = \pi r^2 + \frac{1}{r}\sqrt{\pi^2 r^6 + 90000}$.
parts.label: i
parts.solution:
Volume: $\dfrac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h = 100 \Rightarrow h = \dfrac{300}{\pi r^2}$
$S = \pi r^2 + \pi r\sqrt{r^2 + h^2} = \pi r^2 + \pi r\sqrt{r^2 + \left(\dfrac{300}{\pi r^2}\right)^2}$
$= \pi r^2 + \pi r\sqrt{\dfrac{\pi^2 r^6 + 90000}{(\pi r^2)^2}}$
$= \pi r^2 + \pi r \cdot \dfrac{\sqrt{\pi^2 r^6 + 90000}}{\pi r^2}$ (since $\pi r^2 > 0$)
$= \pi r^2 + \dfrac{1}{r}\sqrt{\pi^2 r^6 + 90000}$ (shown)

parts.text: Sketch the graph of $S$ for $r > 0$. Hence write down the value of $r$ and find the corresponding value of $h$ which will give the smallest $S$, giving your answers correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.label: ii
parts.solution:
Sketching $S = \pi r^2 + \dfrac{1}{r}\sqrt{\pi^2 r^6 + 90000}$ for $r > 0$ (with vertical asymptote $r = 0$), the curve has a minimum point at $(3.2320, 131.27)$.
From the GC, the minimum $S$ occurs at $r = 3.2320 = 3.23$ cm (3 s.f.).
Corresponding $h = \dfrac{300}{\pi (3.2320)^2} = 9.14$ cm (3 s.f.).

parts.text: A special edition of the Tasty Cone will include a mystery flavour in the shape of a sphere inscribed in the cone as shown in Fig. 2. The sphere has centre $O$ and radius $2$ cm. The cross-section of the cone is shown in Fig. 3, where $A$ is a point of contact of the sphere with the cone. Show that $r^2 = \frac{4h}{h - 4}$.
parts.label: iii
parts.solution:
By similar triangles ($\triangle EAO$ and $\triangle EFC$):
$\dfrac{r}{2} = \dfrac{\sqrt{r^2 + h^2}}{h - 2}$
$r(h - 2) = 2\sqrt{r^2 + h^2}$
$r^2(h - 2)^2 = 4(r^2 + h^2)$
$r^2(h^2 - 4h + 4) = 4r^2 + 4h^2$
$r^2 h^2 - 4hr^2 + 4r^2 = 4r^2 + 4h^2$
$r^2 h^2 - 4hr^2 = 4h^2$
$r^2 h(h - 4) = 4h^2$
$\therefore r^2 = \dfrac{4h}{h - 4}$ (shown)

parts.text: Use differentiation to find the exact values of $h$ and $r$ which will give the smallest volume of the cone in the special edition.
parts.label: iv
parts.solution:
$V = \dfrac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h = \dfrac{1}{3}\pi\left(\dfrac{4h}{h - 4}\right)h = \dfrac{4\pi h^2}{3(h - 4)}$
$\dfrac{dV}{dh} = \dfrac{4\pi}{3} \cdot \dfrac{(h - 4)(2h) - h^2}{(h - 4)^2} = \dfrac{4\pi}{3} \cdot \dfrac{h^2 - 8h}{(h - 4)^2} = \dfrac{4\pi h(h - 8)}{3(h - 4)^2}$
For stationary $V$, $\dfrac{dV}{dh} = 0 \Rightarrow h = 0$ (rejected) or $h = 8$.
For $h$ near $8$, $(h - 4)^2 > 0$ and $h > 0$, so the sign of $\dfrac{dV}{dh}$ follows that of $(h - 8)$: negative for $h < 8$, positive for $h > 8$. Hence $V$ is a minimum at $h = 8$.
$r^2 = \dfrac{4(8)}{8 - 4} = 8 \Rightarrow r = 2\sqrt{2}$
$\therefore h = 8$ and $r = 2\sqrt{2}$ give the smallest volume of the cone in the special edition.

stem: Here is some information about a grain storage bin. In this question, the grain storage bin can be modelled as a right cylinder with a right conical top. The height of the conical top is half the radius of the bin.

parts.text: Work out the area, in square metres, of the base of the grain storage bin.
parts.label: a
parts.solution:
Diameter $= 4550$ mm $= 4.55$ m, so radius $r = 2.275$ m.
Base area $= \pi r^2 = \pi (2.275)^2 = 16.3$ m$^2$.

parts.text: Work out the volume, in cubic metres, of the grain storage bin.
parts.label: b
parts.solution:
Radius $r = 2.275$ m. Height of conical top $= \frac{1}{2}r = 1.1375$ m.
Total height $= 6880$ mm $= 6.88$ m, so cylinder height $= 6.88 - 1.1375 = 5.7425$ m.
Volume of cylinder $= \pi r^2 h = \pi(2.275)^2(5.7425) = 93.37$ m$^3$.
Volume of cone $= \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h = \frac{1}{3}\pi(2.275)^2(1.1375) = 6.17$ m$^3$.
Total volume $= 93.37 + 6.17 = 99.5$ m$^3$.

parts.text: The storage bin is never filled to more than its safe volume. It will need a special load-bearing support structure if its total weight per square metre, on the ground beneath, is greater than $20$ kN/m$^2$. Given that the model is an underestimation of the actual storage capacity of the bin, does the bin need a special load-bearing support structure? Justify your decision with calculations.
parts.label: c
parts.answer: Yes. Load per square metre $\approx 21.6$ kN/m$^2 > 20$ kN/m$^2$; since the model underestimates actual capacity, a special load-bearing support structure is needed.
parts.solution:
Safe volume $= 85\% \times 99.536 = 84.6$ m$^3$.
Mass of grain $= 84.6 \times 410 = 34688$ kg.
Total mass (grain $+$ bin) $= 34688 + 1100 = 35788$ kg.
Weight $= \frac{35788}{1000} \times 9.81 = 351.08$ kN.
Load per square metre on the ground $= \frac{351.08}{16.26} = 21.6$ kN/m$^2$.
Since $21.6$ kN/m$^2 > 20$ kN/m$^2$, and the model underestimates the actual capacity (so the real load is even greater), the bin needs a special load-bearing support structure.

stem: A shop sells yoghurt in cups as shown in Figure 1. The cup can be modelled as a frustum, which is a part of a right circular cone, as shown in Figure 2. The top of the cup is a circle of radius $5$ cm. The base of the cup is a circle of radius $2$ cm. The height of the cup is $9$ cm. All dimensions are given in centimetres.

parts.text: Show that the value of $x$ is $6$.
parts.label: a

parts.text: Find the volume of the frustum.
parts.label: b

parts.text: A plastic packaging will be printed around the side of the yoghurt cup. Each cm$^{2}$ of plastic packaging costs $0.1$ cents. Find the cost of the plastic packaging for each yoghurt cup in dollars. Leave your answer to two decimal places.
parts.label: c
parts.solution:
Slant height of larger cone
$= \sqrt{15^2 + 5^2}$
$= \sqrt{250}$

Slant height of smaller cone
$= \sqrt{6^2 + 2^2}$
$= \sqrt{40}$

Curved surface area of frustum
$= \pi(5)(\sqrt{250}) - \pi(2)(\sqrt{40})$
$= 208.6263536$

Cost
$= 208.6263536 \times \dfrac{0.1}{100}$
$= \$0.2086263536$
$= \$0.21$ ($2$ dp)

parts.text: The shop also sells yoghurt in a bowl. The bowl can be modelled as a hemisphere with radius $5$ cm. The prices for the yoghurt are $\$1.80$ for the cup and $\$1.60$ for the bowl. Determine if the yoghurt sold in a cup or a bowl is a better buy.
parts.label: d
parts.answer: The cup is the better buy: $\approx 204.4$ cm$^{3}$ per dollar for the cup vs $\approx 163.6$ cm$^{3}$ per dollar for the bowl.
parts.solution:
Volume of hemisphere bowl
$= \dfrac{2}{3}\pi(5)^3$
$= 261.7993878$ cm$^3$

Amount of yoghurt per $\$$ (in cup)
$= 367.5663405 \div 1.80$
$= 204.2035$ cm$^3$ / $\$$

Amount of yoghurt per $\$$ (in bowl)
$= 261.7993878 \div 1.60$
$= 163.6246$ cm$^3$ / $\$$

Yoghurt in a cup is a better buy because there is more yoghurt per dollar paid.

stem: In the following diagrams, find the value of angle $x$. Write the reasons clearly.

parts.text: In the first diagram, $AB$, $CD$ and $EFG$ are parallel lines, $AF$ and $CF$ are straight lines meeting $EFG$ at $F$, $\angle BAF = 43^{\circ}$ and $\angle DCF = 114^{\circ}$. Find $x = \angle AFC$.
parts.label: a
parts.solution:
$\angle AFE = \angle BAF = 43^{\circ}$ (alternate angles, $AB \parallel EG$)
$\angle CFG = 180^{\circ} - \angle DCF = 180^{\circ} - 114^{\circ} = 66^{\circ}$ (interior angles, $CD \parallel EG$)
$x = 180^{\circ} - \angle AFE - \angle CFG$ (angles on a straight line $EFG$)
$x = 180^{\circ} - 43^{\circ} - 66^{\circ} = 71^{\circ}$

parts.text: In the second diagram, $POS$, $TOQ$ and $UOR$ are straight lines meeting at $O$, $\angle POQ = 70^{\circ}$, $\angle UOT = 2x$ and $\angle ROS = 2x$. Find $x$.
parts.label: b
parts.solution:
$\angle UOP = \angle ROS = 2x$ (vertically opposite angles)
$\angle QOR = \angle UOT = 2x$ (vertically opposite angles)
$\angle UOP + \angle POQ + \angle QOR = 180^{\circ}$ (angles on a straight line $UOR$)
$2x + 70^{\circ} + 2x = 180^{\circ}$
$4x = 110^{\circ}$
$x = 27.5^{\circ}$

stem: Instructions for baking a heart-shaped cake: bake a square cake of side $20$ cm; bake two semicircle cakes of radius $10$ cm; join the two halves to the square cake, as shown in the diagram.

parts.text: Find the area of the top view of the cake.
parts.label: a

parts.text: A red ribbon is fixed around the sides for the heart-shaped cake with the sides overlapping by $3$ cm. Find the length of ribbon required.
parts.label: b
parts.solution:
Perimeter of cake $= 2(20) + 2\pi(10) = (40 + 20\pi)$ cm
Length of ribbon required $= 40 + 20\pi + 3$
$= 106$ cm

stem: Solid $A$ shows a solid formed by joining a hemisphere of radius $r$ to one end of a cylinder of height $r$. The other end of the cylinder is attached to a cone of height $h$ cm.

parts.text: Find, in terms of $\pi$ and $r$, the total volume of the hemisphere and cylinder.
parts.label: a
parts.solution: Volume $= \dfrac{2}{3}\pi r^{3} + \pi r^{2}(r) = \dfrac{2}{3}\pi r^{3} + \pi r^{3} = \dfrac{5}{3}\pi r^{3}$

parts.text: The volume of the cone is half of the volume of the entire Solid $A$. Show that $h = 5r$.
parts.label: b
parts.solution:
The cone's volume is half of the total volume of Solid $A$:
$\dfrac{1}{3}\pi r^{2} h = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{5}{3}\pi r^{3} + \dfrac{1}{3}\pi r^{2} h\right)$
$\dfrac{2}{3}\pi r^{2} h = \dfrac{5}{3}\pi r^{3} + \dfrac{1}{3}\pi r^{2} h$
$\dfrac{1}{3}\pi r^{2} h = \dfrac{5}{3}\pi r^{3}$
$h = 5r$ (shown)

parts.text: Given that the volume of the hemisphere is $54\pi$ cm$^{3}$, find the volume of Solid $A$.
parts.label: c

parts.text: The whole Solid $A$ is then melted down to form a prism, Solid $B$. The cross-section is a trapezium with the parallel sides measuring 6 cm and 10 cm. Find $y$, the height of the cross-section of Solid $B$.
parts.label: d

stem: The diagram shows the speed-time graph of an object which travels at a constant speed of $24$ m/s for $6$ seconds before slowing down at a rate of $2$ m/s$^{2}$ and coming to a rest after $t$ seconds.

parts.text: Find the value of $t$.
parts.label: a
parts.solution:
The deceleration line has gradient $-2$:
$\dfrac{24 - 0}{6 - t} = -2$
$24 = -2(6 - t)$
$24 = -12 + 2t$
$2t = 36$
$t = 18$

parts.text: Calculate the average speed for the whole journey.
parts.label: b
parts.solution:
Total distance $= (6 \times 24) + \left(\dfrac{1}{2} \times 12 \times 24\right)$
$= 144 + 144$
$= 288$ m
Average speed $= \dfrac{288}{18} = 16$ m/s

parts.text: Sketch the distance-time graph of the object for the whole journey on the axes below.
parts.label: c
parts.answer: Straight line from $(0, 0)$ to $(6, 144)$ (constant speed), then concave curve from $(6, 144)$ to $(18, 288)$ (decelerating), ending horizontally at rest.
parts.solution: Distance-time graph: a straight line from $(0, 0)$ to $(6, 144)$ (constant speed), then a concave-down curve from $(6, 144)$ to $(18, 288)$ which flattens to horizontal at $(18, 288)$ as the object comes to rest.

stem: The diagram below shows the cross-section of a door knob. The curved part of the door knob can be modelled by the curve $C$ with equation $y = \dfrac{2x}{1 + x^2}$ between $x = 0$ and $x = 2$. The solid door knob is obtained by rotating $C$ through four right angles about the $x$-axis. The exterior and the interior of the door knob are made of wood and plastic respectively. The interior of the door knob consists of a solid cone.

parts.text: Sketch the graph of $C$ for $0 \leq x \leq 2$.
parts.label: i
parts.answer: Curve from the origin rising to a maximum at $(1,1)$, then decreasing to $\left(2,\dfrac{4}{5}\right)$.
parts.solution: $y=\dfrac{2x}{1+x^2}$ passes through $(0,0)$, has a maximum at $x=1$ giving $(1,1)$, then decreases to $\left(2,\dfrac{4}{5}\right)$.

parts.text: Using the substitution $x = \tan\theta$, find the exact volume of the door knob.
parts.label: ii
parts.solution:
$V=\pi\displaystyle\int_0^2 \dfrac{4x^2}{(1+x^2)^2}\,dx$. With $x=\tan\theta,\ dx=\sec^2\theta\,d\theta,\ 1+x^2=\sec^2\theta$, limits $0\to\tan^{-1}2$:
$=4\pi\displaystyle\int_0^{\tan^{-1}2}\sin^2\theta\,d\theta=2\pi\left[\theta-\dfrac{\sin2\theta}{2}\right]_0^{\tan^{-1}2}$.
At $\theta=\tan^{-1}2$: $\sin2\theta=\dfrac{4}{5}$, so $V=2\pi\left(\tan^{-1}2-\dfrac{2}{5}\right)$.

parts.text: The cost of wood and plastic used in manufacturing the door knob is $\$3$ and $\$1.20$ per unit volume respectively. The interior of the door knob consists of a solid cone. Find the cost of manufacturing one such door knob, giving your answer to the nearest dollar.
parts.label: iii
parts.solution:
Cone interior: base radius $y(2)=\dfrac{4}{5}$, height $2$; volume $=\dfrac13\pi\left(\dfrac45\right)^2(2)=\dfrac{32\pi}{75}\approx1.340$.
Total solid $V=2\pi\left(\tan^{-1}2-\dfrac25\right)\approx4.443$; wood $=V-\text{cone}\approx3.103$.
Cost $=3(3.103)+1.20(1.340)\approx9.31+1.61=\$10.9\approx\$11$.

stem: The diagram shows the speed-time graph of a particle.

parts.text: Find the speed of the particle when $t=12$ s.
parts.label: a
parts.solution:
Let the speed of the particle when $t=12$ be $v$.
$\dfrac{v-30}{12-6} = \dfrac{100-30}{13-6}$
$\therefore v = 90$ m/s

parts.text: Find the distance covered before the particle starts to slow down.
parts.label: b
parts.solution:
Distance = Area under the graph from $0$ s to $13$ s
$= (6)(30)+\dfrac{1}{2}(30+100)(13-6)$
$= 635$ m

parts.text: Complete the distance-time graph of the particle.
parts.label: c
parts.answer: Distance-time graph: curve rising (accel phase), then straight line with constant positive gradient during constant speed, then concave down during deceleration.
parts.solution: Distance-time graph: from $t=0$ to $6$ a straight line of constant positive gradient (constant speed 30 m/s); from $t=6$ to $13$ a curve of increasing gradient (speeding up); from $t=13$ to $21$ a curve of decreasing gradient (slowing down), reaching the maximum distance at $t=21$.

stem: In triangle $ABC$, angle $ABC$ is $15^\circ$, $AB$ is 20 cm, and $AC$ is 10 cm.

parts.text: Find angle $ACB$.
parts.label: a
parts.solution:
By the sine rule: $\frac{\sin \angle ACB}{20} = \frac{\sin 15^\circ}{10}$
$\sin \angle ACB = 2\sin 15^\circ = 0.5176...$
$\angle ACB = 31.2^\circ$ (rejected, from the diagram $\angle ACB$ is obtuse) or $148.8^\circ$
$\angle ACB = 148.8^\circ$

parts.text: Find angle $BAC$.
parts.label: b
parts.solution: $\angle BAC = 180^\circ-15^\circ-148.8^\circ = 16.2^\circ$

parts.text: Find the area of triangle $ABC$.
parts.label: c

parts.solution:
Area $= \frac{1}{2} \times AB \times h$

parts.text: The point $C$ is now moved to point $D$, such that $BD$ is 25 cm. Show that angle $BAD$ is approximately $108.2^\circ$.

stem: The diagram shows Solid A consisting of a right circular cone attached to a hemisphere with a common circular base of radius $r$ cm. The height of the cone is $24$ cm. The volume of the cone is equal to twice the volume of the hemisphere.

parts.text: Show that $r = 6$. [2]
parts.label: a
parts.solution:
Volume of cone $= 2 \times$ Volume of hemisphere
$\dfrac{1}{3}\pi r^2 (24) = 2 \times \dfrac{2}{3}\pi r^3$
$24 = 4r$
$r = 6$. (Shown.)

parts.text: Solid $\mathbf{B}$ is constructed by removing a smaller cone of base radius $x$ cm and height $y$ cm.
parts.label: b

subparts.text: Find the value of $\dfrac{x}{y}$. [1]
subparts.label: i
subparts.solution: By similar triangles, $\dfrac{x}{y} = \dfrac{6}{24} = \dfrac{1}{4}$ or $\dfrac{x}{6} = \dfrac{y}{24}$.

subparts.text: Given that the volume of the cone removed is $121.5\pi$ cm$^3$, calculate the total surface area of Solid B. [5]
subparts.label: ii
subparts.solution:
$\dfrac{x}{y} = \dfrac{1}{4} \Rightarrow y = 4x$.
$\dfrac{1}{3}\pi x^2 y = 121.5\pi \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{3}\pi x^2 (4x) = 121.5\pi \Rightarrow x^3 = \dfrac{729}{8} \Rightarrow x = \dfrac{9}{2}$.
Slant height of big cone $= \sqrt{24^2 + 6^2} = \sqrt{612}$.
Slant height of small cone $= \sqrt{18^2 + (9/2)^2} = \sqrt{344.25}$.
Curved surface area of remaining solid $= \pi(6)(\sqrt{612}) - \pi(9/2)(\sqrt{344.25}) = 204.01$.
Curved surface area of hemisphere $= 2\pi(6)^2 = 72\pi$.
Total surface area $= 72\pi + \pi(9/2)^2 + 204.01 = 494$ cm$^2$ (to 3 s.f.).

stem: The diagram shows the speed-time graph for a car journey. The total distance travelled by the car is $504$ m.

parts.text: Convert the constant speed of the car during the journey into km/h.
parts.label: a
parts.solution: $24$ m/s $= \dfrac{24 \times \tfrac{1}{1000}\,\text{km}}{1 \times \tfrac{1}{3600}\,\text{h}} = 86.4$ km/h.

parts.text: Calculate the greatest speed, $v$ m/s, of the car.
parts.label: b
parts.solution:
Total distance $504$ m is the area under the speed-time graph:
$504 = \left(\tfrac{1}{2} \times 5 \times v\right) + \left(\tfrac{1}{2}(v + 24)(7)\right) + \left(\tfrac{1}{2}(8 + 12)(24)\right)$
$504 = \tfrac{5}{2}v + \tfrac{7}{2}v + 84 + 240$
$180 = 6v \Rightarrow v = 30$ m/s.

parts.text: Sketch the distance-time graph for the entire journey.
parts.label: c
parts.answer: A continuous piecewise curve: parabolic portion during acceleration, straight-line portion during constant speed, and curve during deceleration; cumulative distance reaches $504$ m at the end.
parts.solution:
Cumulative distances:
Distance from $0$ s to $5$ s $= \tfrac{1}{2} \times 5 \times 30 = 75$ m.
Distance from $0$ s to $12$ s $= 75 + \tfrac{1}{2}(30 + 24)(7) = 264$ m.
Distance from $0$ s to $20$ s $= 264 + (24)(8) = 456$ m.
Distance from $0$ s to $24$ s $= 456 + \tfrac{1}{2}(24)(4) = 504$ m.
Sketch: curved (concave-up) section from $(0, 0)$ to $(5, 75)$, straight line of constant gradient from $(5, 75)$ to $(12, 264)$, another straight line from $(12, 264)$ to $(20, 456)$, then curved (concave-down) section from $(20, 456)$ to $(24, 504)$.

stem: The diagram shows a right circular cone cut from a solid steel sphere. Point $O$ is the centre of the sphere with radius $12\text{ cm}$.

parts.text: Given the circumference of the base of the cone is $50\text{ cm}$, show that the height of the cone is $21.0\text{ cm}$, corrected to $3$ significant figures.
parts.label: a
parts.answer: Radius of base $= \dfrac{50}{2\pi} \approx 7.9577\text{ cm}$. Height $= 12 + \sqrt{12^{2} - 7.9577^{2}} = 12 + 8.973 \approx 20.97 \approx 21.0\text{ cm}$ (to $3$ s.f.). (Shown)
parts.solution:
Radius of cone $= \dfrac{50}{2\pi} = 7.9577\text{ cm}$
Length from $O$ to base of cone $= \sqrt{12^{2}-7.9577^{2}} = 8.9819\text{ cm}$
Height of cone $= 12+8.9819 = 20.9819 = 21.0\text{ cm}$ (to 3 s.f.)

parts.text: Find the curved surface area of the cone.
parts.label: b
parts.solution:
Slant height of cone $= \sqrt{20.9819^{2}+7.9577^{2}} = 22.440\text{ cm}$
Curved surface area $= \pi(7.9577)(22.440) = 561\text{ cm}^{2}$ (to 3 s.f.)

parts.text: After the cone is cut from the steel sphere, the remaining steel is melted down to form part of a solid right circular cone as shown in the following diagram. The cone comprises $3$ layers of equal heights, $h\text{ cm}$. The top and bottom layers are cast from the remaining steel. The centre section is made from acrylic. Find the volume of the acrylic used to make the centre layer of the solid cone.
parts.label: c
parts.solution:
Volume of cone in sphere $= \dfrac{1}{3}\pi(7.9577)^{2}(20.9819) = 1391.4\text{ cm}^{3}$
Volume of remaining steel $= \dfrac{4}{3}\pi(12)^{3}-1391.4 = 5846.8\text{ cm}^{3}$
Ratio of volumes $A : (A+B) : (A+B+C) = h^{3} : (2h)^{3} : (3h)^{3} = 1 : 8 : 27$.
The two steel layers (top and bottom) form $A+C = 27-7 = 20$ parts; the acrylic middle layer is $B = 7$ parts.
Volume of acrylic $= \dfrac{7}{20}\times 5846.8 = 2050\text{ cm}^{3}$ (to 3 s.f.)

stem: A conical container with a diameter of 10 cm and a height of 8 cm is filled with water to a depth of 4 cm.

parts.text: Show that the volume of the water in the container is $\dfrac{25}{3}\pi$ cm$^3$.
parts.label: a
parts.solution:
Let the radius of the water surface be $r$ cm.
$\dfrac{r}{5} = \dfrac{4}{8}$
$r = \dfrac{5}{2}$
$\therefore$ volume of water $= \dfrac{1}{3}\pi\left(\dfrac{5}{2}\right)^2 \times 4$
$= \dfrac{25}{3}\pi$ cm$^3$ (Shown)

parts.text: Find the surface area of the inside of the container that is in contact with the water.
parts.label: b
parts.solution:
Surface area $= \pi r l$
$= \pi\left(\dfrac{5}{2}\right)\sqrt{4^2 + \left(\dfrac{5}{2}\right)^2}$
$= 37.04716$ cm$^2$
$\approx 37.0$ cm$^2$

parts.text: The water in the cone is poured into a test tube. The test tube is made by joining together a cylinder of diameter 3 cm and a hemisphere of diameter 3 cm. Calculate the height of the water in the test tube.
parts.label: c
parts.solution:
Let the height of the water above the hemisphere be $h$ cm.
$\pi\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)^2 h + \dfrac{2}{3}\pi\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)^3 = \dfrac{25}{3}\pi$
$\dfrac{9}{4}h = \dfrac{73}{12}$
$h = 2\dfrac{19}{27}$ cm
$\therefore$ height of water in the test tube $= h + \dfrac{3}{2}$

stem: The diagram shows the positions of three buildings $P$, $Q$ and $R$ in a school. $R$ is $196$ m from $P$ on a bearing of $048°$. $Q$ is $176$ m from $R$ on a bearing of $155°$.

parts.text: Show that $PQ = 222$ m, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.label: a

parts.text: Calculate the bearing of $P$ from $Q$.
parts.label: b
parts.solution:
$\dfrac{\sin \angle PQR}{196} = \dfrac{\sin \angle PRQ}{PQ}$
$\sin \angle PQR = \dfrac{196\sin 73^\circ}{221.85736\ldots}$
$\angle PQR = 57.65564\ldots^\circ$
Bearing of $P$ from $Q = 360^\circ - \angle PQR - (180^\circ - 155^\circ)$ (angles at a point)
$= 360^\circ - 57.65564\ldots^\circ - 25^\circ$
$= 277.34436\ldots^\circ$
$= 277.3^\circ$ (1 d.p.)

parts.text: The diagram below shows a scale drawing of the positions of the three buildings $P$, $Q$ and $R$ in the same school.
parts.label: c

subparts.text: On the diagram, construct the bisector of angle $PQR$.
subparts.label: i
subparts.solution: The angle bisector of $\angle PQR$ is constructed (using arcs from $Q$).

subparts.text: A new building, $S$, will be added to the school. $S$ is to be equidistant from $Q$ and from $R$. By making a suitable construction, show the possible positions of $S$ on the diagram.
subparts.label: ii
subparts.answer: Perpendicular bisector of $QR$ drawn; $S$ lies on this line.
subparts.solution: The perpendicular bisector of $QR$ is constructed; $S$ lies on this line, since $S$ is equidistant from $Q$ and $R$.

subparts.text: Given further that $S$ is equidistant from $PQ$ and from $QR$, find the actual distance of $S$ from $P$.

subparts.solution:
$S$ is the intersection of the angle bisector of $\angle PQR$ and the perpendicular bisector of $QR$.
Distance on the diagram $= 7.1$ cm.
Actual distance $= 7.1 \times 20 = 142$ m

stem: A fish tank manufacturer makes an open fish tank in a shape of a cuboid with internal breadth, length and height of $x$ cm, $2x$ cm and $y$ cm respectively (see diagram). The manufacturer determines that the internal volume of the tank must be $36\,000$ cm$^3$ and the total internal surface area of the tank, $A$ cm$^2$, should be as small as possible.

parts.text: Find a formula for $A$ in terms of $x$. Hence show that for $A$ to be minimum, the breadth, length and height of the tank are 30 cm, 60 cm and 20 cm respectively.
parts.label: i
parts.answer: $A = 2x^2 + \dfrac{108000}{x}$; minimum at $x = 30$, giving breadth 30 cm, length 60 cm, height 20 cm.
parts.solution:
$2x^2 y = 36000 \Rightarrow y = \dfrac{18000}{x^2}$
$A = 6xy + 2x^2 = 6x\left(\dfrac{18000}{x^2}\right) + 2x^2 = \dfrac{108000}{x} + 2x^2$
$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}A}{\mathrm{d}x} = -\dfrac{108000}{x^2} + 4x$
Set $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}A}{\mathrm{d}x} = 0$: $\dfrac{108000}{x^2} = 4x \Rightarrow x^3 = 27000 \Rightarrow x = 30$.
$y = \dfrac{18000}{30^2} = 20$.
$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}^2 A}{\mathrm{d}x^2} = \dfrac{216000}{x^3} + 4$; at $x = 30$, $= 8 + 4 = 12 > 0$ (minimum).
Therefore breadth $= x = 30$ cm, length $= 2x = 60$ cm and height $= y = 20$ cm. (shown)

parts.text: A fish tank of dimension found in part (i) is built and is placed on a horizontal shelf. A solid cone with height 20 cm has its circular base with radius 5 cm attached to the internal rectangular base of the fish tank (see diagram). Water is poured at a constant rate of 1000 cm$^3$ per second into the tank. At time $t$ seconds after the start, the height of the water level in the tank is $h$ cm and the volume of water is $V$ cm$^3$. [The volume of a cone of base radius $r$ and height $h$ is given by $V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h$.]
parts.label: ii

subparts.text: Show that for $h < 20$, $$V = 1800h - \frac{\pi}{48}\left[8000 - (20 - h)^3\right].$$
subparts.label: a
subparts.solution:
By similar triangles, the radius $r$ of the cone at the water surface satisfies $\dfrac{r}{5} = \dfrac{20 - h}{20}$, so $r = \dfrac{20 - h}{4}$.
Volume of cone below the water level $= \dfrac{1}{3}\pi(5)^2(20) - \dfrac{1}{3}\pi r^2(20 - h)$
$= \dfrac{500}{3}\pi - \dfrac{1}{3}\pi\left(\dfrac{20 - h}{4}\right)^2(20 - h) = \dfrac{500}{3}\pi - \dfrac{1}{48}\pi(20 - h)^3 = \dfrac{\pi}{48}\left[8000 - (20 - h)^3\right]$.
$V = \text{(volume of tank to height } h) - \text{(volume of cone below water)}$
$= 30 \times 60 \times h - \dfrac{\pi}{48}\left[8000 - (20 - h)^3\right] = 1800h - \dfrac{\pi}{48}\left[8000 - (20 - h)^3\right]$ (shown)

subparts.text: Find the rate of increase of the water level when it is at a height of 10 cm.
subparts.label: b
subparts.solution:
$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}V}{\mathrm{d}h} = 1800 - \dfrac{\pi}{48}\left[3(20 - h)^2\right] = 1800 - \dfrac{\pi}{16}(20 - h)^2$
When $h = 10$: $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}V}{\mathrm{d}h} = 1800 - \dfrac{\pi}{16}(100)$.
$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}h}{\mathrm{d}t} = \dfrac{\mathrm{d}h}{\mathrm{d}V}\cdot\dfrac{\mathrm{d}V}{\mathrm{d}t} = \dfrac{1000}{1800 - \frac{\pi}{16}(100)} = 0.562$ (3 s.f.)
Therefore the rate of increase of the water level is $0.562$ cm/s.

stem: Fig. 1 shows a rectangular prism. Fig. 2 shows the prism with a removed part that was cut along the plane $ABFE$. The resulting object has a base $ABCD$, a top $EFGH$, a side $CDHG$, and a slanted side $ABFE$. The following information is given. The top $EFGH$ is a part of the plane with equation $4x + y - z = -6$. The base $ABCD$ is a part of the plane with equation $4x + y - z = 7$. The slanted side $ABFE$ is a part of the plane with equation $3x + 4y + 9z = 15$.

parts.text: Find the acute angle between the base and the slanted side.
parts.label: i
parts.solution:
Base: $\mathbf{r}\cdot\begin{pmatrix}4\\1\\-1\end{pmatrix}=7$
Slanted: $\mathbf{r}\cdot\begin{pmatrix}3\\4\\9\end{pmatrix}=15$
$\cos\theta=\dfrac{\left\lvert\begin{pmatrix}4\\1\\-1\end{pmatrix}\cdot\begin{pmatrix}3\\4\\9\end{pmatrix}\right\rvert}{\left\lvert\begin{pmatrix}4\\1\\-1\end{pmatrix}\right\rvert\left\lvert\begin{pmatrix}3\\4\\9\end{pmatrix}\right\rvert}$
$=\left\lvert\dfrac{12+4-9}{\sqrt{16+1+1}\,\sqrt{9+16+81}}\right\rvert$
$=\dfrac{7}{\sqrt{18}\,\sqrt{106}}$
$\theta=80.8^\circ$ (1 d.p.)

parts.text: Find the height of the object, measured in the direction perpendicular to the base.
parts.label: ii
parts.solution:
Method 1 (distance between 2 planes):
Top: $\mathbf{r}\cdot\begin{pmatrix}4\\1\\-1\end{pmatrix}=-6$
Base: $\mathbf{r}\cdot\begin{pmatrix}4\\1\\-1\end{pmatrix}=7$
Height of object $=\left\lvert\dfrac{7-(-6)}{\sqrt{4^2+1^2+1^2}}\right\rvert=\dfrac{13}{\sqrt{18}}=\dfrac{13}{6}\sqrt{2}$ m
Method 2 (length of projection):
$P(0,0,6)$ lies on the top plane and $Q(0,7,0)$ lies on the base plane.
$\overrightarrow{PQ}=\begin{pmatrix}0\\7\\0\end{pmatrix}-\begin{pmatrix}0\\0\\6\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}0\\7\\-6\end{pmatrix}$
Height $=$ length of projection of $\overrightarrow{PQ}$ onto the normal of the base $=\left\lvert\dfrac{\begin{pmatrix}0\\7\\-6\end{pmatrix}\cdot\begin{pmatrix}4\\1\\-1\end{pmatrix}}{\sqrt{4^2+1^2+1^2}}\right\rvert=\dfrac{13}{\sqrt{18}}=\dfrac{13}{6}\sqrt{2}$ m

parts.text: Find a vector equation of the line of intersection between the base and the slanted side.
parts.label: iii
parts.solution:
Base: $4x+y-z=7$
Slanted: $3x+4y+9z=15$
Using GC, the line of intersection is $\mathbf{r}=\begin{pmatrix}1\\3\\0\end{pmatrix}+\lambda\begin{pmatrix}1\\-3\\1\end{pmatrix}$, $\lambda\in\mathbb{R}$.

parts.text: Point $S$ with coordinates $(2, 11, 12)$ lies on $CD$. Find the position vector of the foot of the perpendicular from point $S$ to the line found in part (iii).
parts.label: iv
parts.solution:
Let $N$ be the foot of perpendicular from $S$ to the line.
Since $N$ lies on the line, $\overrightarrow{ON}=\begin{pmatrix}1+\lambda\\3-3\lambda\\\lambda\end{pmatrix}$ for some $\lambda\in\mathbb{R}$.
$\overrightarrow{SN}\cdot\begin{pmatrix}1\\-3\\1\end{pmatrix}=0$
$\left[\begin{pmatrix}1+\lambda\\3-3\lambda\\\lambda\end{pmatrix}-\begin{pmatrix}2\\11\\12\end{pmatrix}\right]\cdot\begin{pmatrix}1\\-3\\1\end{pmatrix}=0$
$\begin{pmatrix}\lambda-1\\-3\lambda-8\\\lambda-12\end{pmatrix}\cdot\begin{pmatrix}1\\-3\\1\end{pmatrix}=0$
$\lambda-1+9\lambda+24+\lambda-12=0$
$11\lambda+11=0$
$\lambda=-1$
Thus $\overrightarrow{ON}=\begin{pmatrix}1-1\\3-3(-1)\\-1\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}0\\6\\-1\end{pmatrix}$

parts.text: A part of the object is to be further removed so that the remaining object is now symmetrical about a plane $p$ that is parallel to $CD$. Fig. 3 shows the remaining object after the removal. Find the cartesian equation of $p$.
parts.label: v
parts.solution:
Position vector of midpoint of $SN=\dfrac{1}{2}\left[\begin{pmatrix}2\\11\\12\end{pmatrix}+\begin{pmatrix}0\\6\\-1\end{pmatrix}\right]=\dfrac{1}{2}\begin{pmatrix}2\\17\\11\end{pmatrix}$
$\overrightarrow{SN}=\begin{pmatrix}2\\11\\12\end{pmatrix}-\begin{pmatrix}0\\6\\-1\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}2\\5\\13\end{pmatrix}$
$\overrightarrow{SN}$ is perpendicular to the required plane $p$, so it is the normal of $p$.
Equation of the plane of symmetry:
$\mathbf{r}\cdot\begin{pmatrix}2\\5\\13\end{pmatrix}=\dfrac{1}{2}\begin{pmatrix}2\\17\\11\end{pmatrix}\cdot\begin{pmatrix}2\\5\\13\end{pmatrix}$
$=\dfrac{1}{2}(4+85+143)$
$=116$
The cartesian equation is $2x+5y+13z=116$.

stem: Ben and Holly would like to take part in a Build a Bench competition using cardboard. They decided to make a bench in the shape of a prism which is hollow in the centre. Ben sketched out Figure $A$, the cross-section of the prism.

parts.text: On the grid, draw an enlargement of Figure $A$ using a scale factor of $\frac{3}{2}$.
parts.label: a
parts.answer: Enlargement of Figure A with scale factor 3/2 drawn correctly on the grid.
parts.solution: Each measurement of Figure $A$ is multiplied by $\frac{3}{2}$, then drawn on the grid. The enlarged cross-section is the same shape with all lengths $1.5$ times the original.

parts.text: Using the enlarged cross-section, Holly made a model of the bench. The model, which takes the shape of a prism, has a volume of $355.5$ cm$^{3}$. Calculate the value of $h$, where $h$ cm is the height of the prism.
parts.label: b
parts.solution:
Area of enlarged cross-section $= \left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^{2} \times $ Area of $A = \frac{9}{4} \times 10 = 22.5$ cm$^{2}$.
Volume of prism $= $ Area of cross-section $\times h$:
$355.5 = 22.5 \times h$
$h = \frac{355.5}{22.5} = 15.8$ cm.

parts.text: After making the model, Ben and Holly started to make the actual bench using cardboard from cardboard boxes. The diagram shows one of the cardboard boxes that they used to make the bench. In the process, $8\%$ of the cardboard boxes are wasted. Suggest a suitable number of such cardboard boxes Ben and Holly will need if they make an actual bench using a scale factor of 10.2 based on the model. Justify your decision and show your calculations clearly.
parts.label: c
parts.answer: They will need 5 cardboard boxes to ensure there is enough material to make the bench (computed $\approx 4.99$ boxes before rounding up).
parts.solution:
Surface area of each cardboard box $= 2(50 \times 40) + 2(50 \times 30) + 2(40 \times 30) = 9400$ cm$^{2}$.
Perimeter of sketch $A$ (from Figure $A$) $= 5 + 2 + \sqrt{4^{2} + 1^{2}} + 2\sqrt{2^{2} + 1^{2}} = 7 + \sqrt{17} + 2\sqrt{5}$ cm.
Perimeter of enlarged figure $= \frac{3}{2}(7 + \sqrt{17} + 2\sqrt{5}) = \frac{21}{2} + \frac{3}{2}\sqrt{17} + 3\sqrt{5}$ cm.
Surface area of model (the prism's lateral surface using the enlarged perimeter, plus 2 cross-section ends)
$= 15.8\left(\frac{21}{2} + \frac{3}{2}\sqrt{17} + 3\sqrt{5}\right) + 2(22.5)$
$\approx 414.6$ cm$^{2}$.
Surface area of actual bench $= 10.2^{2} \times 414.6072\ldots \approx 43\,135.7$ cm$^{2}$.
Account for 8% wastage: effective cardboard per box $= 0.92 \times 9400 = 8648$ cm$^{2}$.
Number of boxes $= \frac{43\,135.7}{0.92 \times 9400} \approx 4.988$.
Round up: they will need 5 cardboard boxes.

stem: The diagram above shows an arch bridge. The arc $AFTEB$ is part of a circle with centre $P$, and $AB$ is a chord 8 m. Point $T$ is 1 m vertically above point $M$ which is the midpoint of $AB$. $CF$ and $DE$ are perpendicular to chord $AB$. The arc $AFTEB$ can be modelled onto the coordinate plane below, where $C$ and $D$ are $(-3, 0)$ and $(3, 0)$ respectively.

parts.text: Show that $P$ is $(0, -7.5)$.
parts.label: i
parts.solution:
Let the centre be $P(0, k)$, which lies on the $y$-axis.
$TP = BP$ (radii), with $T(0, 1)$ and $B(4, 0)$:
$(1 - k)^2 = (4 - 0)^2 + (0 - k)^2$
$1 - 2k + k^2 = 16 + k^2$
$-2k = 15 \Rightarrow k = -7.5$
$\therefore P(0, -7.5)$ (shown)

parts.text: Find the equation of tangent at point $B$.

parts.solution:
$PB$ is perpendicular to the tangent at $B$.
Gradient of $PB = \dfrac{0 - (-7.5)}{4 - 0} = \dfrac{7.5}{4} = \dfrac{15}{8}$
Gradient of tangent at $B = -\dfrac{8}{15}$
Equation: $y - 0 = -\dfrac{8}{15}(x - 4)$
$y = -\dfrac{8}{15}x + \dfrac{32}{15}$
$\therefore 15y = -8x + 32$
