Since $S\$1 = \pounds 0.55$, cost $= \frac{0.72}{0.55} = 1.3090...$
Cost of one sheet $= S\$1.31$ (to the nearest cent).

parts.text: Ali was to make an open recycle bin with cardboard in the shape of a prism with a square base. The uniform cross-section of the prism is a trapezium $WXYZ$ with height $70$ cm, $XY = 30$ cm, $WZ = 50$ cm and $WX = 70.71$ cm. Calculate the total area of cardboard to be used for this bin.
parts.label: b
parts.solution:
The base $XY$ is a square of side $30$ cm, so the prism is $30$ cm long.
Two trapezium faces: $2 \times \frac{1}{2}(30 + 50)(70) = 2 \times 2800 = 5600$ cm$^{2}$
Square base: $30 \times 30 = 900$ cm$^{2}$
Two slanting rectangular faces: $2 \times (70.71 \times 30) = 4242.6$ cm$^{2}$
The bin is open, so no top is needed.
Total area of cardboard $= 5600 + 900 + 4242.6 = 10742.6$ cm$^{2}$

parts.text: If Ali had used one sheet of the cardboard mentioned in (a) to make the bin, calculate the percentage of wasted cardboard.
parts.label: c
parts.solution:
One sheet is $1000$ mm by $1200$ mm, i.e. $100$ cm by $120$ cm.
Area of one sheet $= 100 \times 120 = 12000$ cm$^{2}$
Cardboard wasted $= 12000 - 10742.6 = 1257.4$ cm$^{2}$
Percentage wasted $= \frac{1257.4}{12000} \times 100\% = 10.478...\% = 10.5\%$ (to 3 significant figures).

stem: The figure shows Soda Can A, which can be modelled as a cylinder of height $12\text{ cm}$ and radius $3\text{ cm}$.

parts.text: Using the model, show that the volume of the Soda Can A is $108\pi\text{ cm}^3$.
parts.label: a
parts.solution: Volume $= \pi r^2 h = \pi(3)^2(12) = \pi \times 9 \times 12 = 108\pi\text{ cm}^3$ (shown)

parts.text: Using the model, estimate the total surface area of the Soda Can A, in $\text{cm}^2$.
parts.label: b
parts.solution:
Total surface area $= 2\pi r^2 + 2\pi r h$
$= 2\pi(3)^2 + 2\pi(3)(12)$
$= 18\pi + 72\pi = 90\pi$
$= 282.74\ldots = 283\text{ cm}^2$ (3 s.f.)

parts.text:
The figure shows another Soda Can B, which can be modelled as a cylinder of height $17.28\text{ cm}$ and radius $2.5\text{ cm}$.
The volume of the Soda Can B is $108\pi\text{ cm}^3$ and its total surface area is $98.9\pi\text{ cm}^2$.
parts.label: c

subparts.text: As a manufacturer of drink cans, which design will you use? Justify your answer.
subparts.label: i
subparts.answer: Soda Can A, as it has a smaller total surface area and hence will be cheaper to manufacture
subparts.solution:
Both cans hold the same volume of $108\pi\text{ cm}^3$.
Can A: total surface area $= 90\pi\text{ cm}^2$
Can B: total surface area $= 98.9\pi\text{ cm}^2$

$90\pi < 98.9\pi$, so Can A uses less material for the same volume and is cheaper to manufacture.
Choose Soda Can A.

subparts.text:
The smaller the volume to surface-area ratio, the faster the soda drink can will cool down in the freezer.
Determine which Soda Can will cool down faster in the freezer. Show your working clearly.
subparts.label: ii
subparts.answer: Soda Can B will cool down faster.
subparts.solution:
Can A: $\frac{\text{volume}}{\text{surface area}} = \frac{108\pi}{90\pi} = 1.2$

Can B: $\frac{\text{volume}}{\text{surface area}} = \frac{108\pi}{98.9\pi} = 1.0919\ldots$

$1.0919\ldots < 1.2$, so Can B has the smaller volume to surface-area ratio.
Soda Can B will cool down faster.

stem:
Concrete solid barriers are used for guiding traffic and securing property from automobile traffic. Figure 1 shows a concrete traffic control barrier.
The barrier can be modelled by a prism with uniform cross section of length 3 m, as shown in Figure 2. The sloping sides $PQAB$ and $SRDC$ are rectangles.
The uniform cross-section of the prism is made up of a trapezium $PQRS$ and a semi-circle with diameter $RQ$.
The perpendicular height between $RQ$ and $SP$ is 0.5 m.
$RQ = 0.2$ m and $SP = 0.6$ m. $SR = PQ = 0.7$ m.

subparts.text: Show that the cross-sectional area of the barrier is $0.2157$ m$^2$, correct to 4 significant figures.
subparts.label: i
subparts.solution:
Area of trapezium $PQRS = \frac{1}{2} \times (0.2 + 0.6) \times 0.5$
$= 0.2$ m$^2$
Radius of semi-circle $= \frac{0.2}{2} = 0.1$ m
Area of semi-circle $= \frac{1}{2} \times \pi \times 0.1^2 = 0.0157079...$ m$^2$
Cross-sectional area $= 0.2 + 0.0157079... = 0.2157079...$
$= 0.2157$ m$^2$ (to 4 s.f.) (shown)

subparts.text: Hence, calculate the volume of the barrier.
subparts.label: ii
subparts.solution:
Volume $=$ cross-sectional area $\times$ length
$= 0.2157 \times 3$
$= 0.6471$
$= 0.647$ m$^3$ (to 3 s.f.)

parts.text: A builder wanted to paint the entire structure excluding the base. A tin of paint can paint an area of 20 m$^2$. Find the maximum number of structure(s) that can be painted with 3 tins of paint.
parts.label: b
parts.solution:
The base is the rectangle $SP \times 3$, which is not painted.
Two cross-sectional faces $= 2 \times 0.2157079... = 0.4314159...$ m$^2$
Rectangles $PQAB$ and $SRDC = 2 \times 0.7 \times 3 = 4.2$ m$^2$
Curved surface of the semi-circular top $= \frac{1}{2} \times \pi \times 0.2 \times 3 = 0.9424777...$ m$^2$
Area to be painted for one barrier $= 0.4314159... + 4.2 + 0.9424777... = 5.5738937...$ m$^2$
Area that 3 tins can paint $= 3 \times 20 = 60$ m$^2$
Number of barriers $= \frac{60}{5.5738937...} = 10.76...$
Maximum number of structures $= 10$

parts.text: The density of the structure is 2.35 g/cm$^3$. The builder's lifting gear can lift a maximum load of 900 kg. Is it safe for the lifting gear to be used to lift the barrier? Justify your decision by showing your working clearly.
parts.label: c
parts.answer: No. Mass of the barrier $= 1520.685$ kg, which is more than 900 kg, so it is not safe.
parts.solution:
Volume $= 0.6471$ m$^3 = 0.6471 \times 1000000 = 647100$ cm$^3$
Mass $= 647100 \times 2.35 = 1520685$ g
$= 1520.685$ kg
Since $1520.685$ kg is more than the maximum load of 900 kg, it is not safe for the lifting gear to be used to lift the barrier.

stem: Jynn wants to make 35 strawberry cookies.

parts.text: How many grams of baking soda will she use?
parts.label: a
parts.solution:
The recipe makes 14 cookies using 5 grams of baking soda.
Number of batches $= \frac{35}{14} = 2.5$
Baking soda needed $= 5 \times 2.5 = 12.5$ grams

parts.text: Each box of strawberry costs $\$8$. How much will Jynn spend on buying strawberries?
parts.label: b
parts.solution:
Strawberries needed $= 1 \times 2.5 = 2.5$ boxes, so she must buy 3 whole boxes.
Cost $= 3 \times \$8 = \$24$

parts.text: Each cookie has a diameter of approximately 5 cm. She packed the cookies into a box with a rectangular base of dimension 17 cm by 28 cm. She used cardboards as partitions to separate layers of cookies. How many cardboards will she need to use as partitions to stack up the cookies?
parts.label: c
parts.solution:
Along the 28 cm side: $28 \div 5 = 5$ cookies (whole cookies only).
Along the 17 cm side: $17 \div 5 = 3$ rows.
Cookies per layer $= 5 \times 3 = 15$
Layers needed $= 15 + 15 + 5$, i.e. 3 layers for 35 cookies.
Partitions between 3 layers $= 3 - 1 = 2$ cardboards

stem: Sketch a straight line graph for the given scenarios, clearly labelling the vertical axis values when the horizontal axis values are 0 and 6 respectively.

parts.text:
The flag down fare of a taxi is $\$3$.
Passengers have to pay $\$0.50$ for each km.
parts.label: a
parts.answer: A straight line from $(0,\ 3)$ to $(6,\ 6)$: vertical axis value $\$3$ at 0 km and $\$6$ at 6 km.
parts.solution:
Fare $= 3 + 0.5d$, where $d$ is the distance in km.
When $d = 0$: fare $= \$3$
When $d = 6$: fare $= 3 + 0.5(6) = \$6$
Draw the straight line joining $(0,\ 3)$ to $(6,\ 6)$.

parts.text:
Carpark A charges: free 20 minutes of parking $+\ \$0.05$ per minute thereafter.
Carpark B charges: single entry charge of $\$12$.
parts.label: b
parts.answer: Carpark A: from $(0,\ 0)$ to $(6,\ 17)$. Carpark B: horizontal line at $\$12$, from $(0,\ 12)$ to $(6,\ 12)$.
parts.solution:
Carpark A: the first 20 minutes are free, then $\$0.05$ per minute.
At 0 hours the charge is $\$0$.
6 hours $= 360$ minutes, of which $360 - 20 = 340$ minutes are charged:
charge $= 340 \times 0.05 = \$17$
So A rises from $(0,\ 0)$ to $(6,\ 17)$.
Carpark B: a flat $\$12$ however long the stay, so B is the horizontal line
from $(0,\ 12)$ to $(6,\ 12)$.

stem: Diagram 1 shows a car porch. The roof of the car porch can be modelled as a square pyramid as shown in Diagram 2.

parts.text: $VA = 5$ m, $AB = 6$ m and $VM$ perpendicular to $AB$. Calculate the surface area of the rooftop.
parts.label: a
parts.solution:
$M$ is the midpoint of $AB$, so $AM = 3$ m.
In $\triangle VAM$, right-angled at $M$:
$VM = \sqrt{5^2 - 3^2} = \sqrt{25 - 9} = \sqrt{16} = 4$ m
Area of $\triangle VAB = \frac{1}{2} \times AB \times VM = \frac{1}{2} \times 6 \times 4 = 12$ m$^2$
The rooftop is made up of 4 identical triangular faces.
Surface area $= 4 \times 12 = 48$ m$^2$

parts.text: The entire rooftop will be reroofed with rectangular tiles. Some information about one tile used is given below. Given that density $= \frac{\text{mass}}{\text{volume}}$ and taking the breadth of each tile as $x$ cm,
parts.label: b

subparts.text: form an equation for the volume and show that it reduces to $x^{2} + 10x - 600 = 0$,
subparts.label: i
subparts.solution:
Volume of one tile $= \frac{\text{mass}}{\text{density}} = \frac{3120}{2.6} = 1200$ cm$^3$
The breadth is $x$ cm and the breadth is $10$ cm less than the length, so the length is $(x + 10)$ cm. The thickness is $2$ cm.
Volume $=$ length $\times$ breadth $\times$ thickness:
$(x + 10)(x)(2) = 1200$
$x(x + 10) = 600$
$x^2 + 10x = 600$
$x^2 + 10x - 600 = 0$ (shown)

subparts.text: hence, calculate the dimensions of each tile.
subparts.label: ii
subparts.solution:
$x^2 + 10x - 600 = 0$
$(x + 30)(x - 20) = 0$
$x = -30$ or $x = 20$
A length cannot be negative, so $x = 20$.
Breadth $= 20$ cm and length $= 20 + 10 = 30$ cm.
Each tile measures $30$ cm by $20$ cm by $2$ cm.

stem: Single-use plastic has a drastic impact on the ecosystem and human health. Plastic straws, like the ones used at Starbucks, have fallen out of favour lately as they are rarely recycled. Given their size and light weight they are often mechanically sorted out during the recycling process and end up in landfills and waterways. It is estimated that 175 million straws are used and then thrown away every day. Starbucks has settled on an alternative to plastic straw use: a new recyclable lid that has a small raised opening allowing consumers to sip their drinks. The new lid can be modelled using a composite shape consisting of a hollow cylindrical base and a trapezoidal prism opening, with a uniform thickness of $0.05$ cm throughout the design. The cylindrical base has an external diameter of $8.5$ cm and a height of $1.0$ cm. The volume of the trapezoidal prism is given to be $0.33$ cm$^3$. The exterior length and width of the trapezoidal prism are $2.5$ cm by $2.0$ cm respectively at the base.

parts.text: Calculate the volume of a new lid using the dimensions given in the model.
parts.label: a
parts.solution:
External radius of the cylindrical base $= \frac{8.5}{2} = 4.25$ cm
Volume of the solid external cylinder $= \pi (4.25)^2 (1.0) = 56.745$ cm$^3$
The wall and base are $0.05$ cm thick, so the hollow cavity has
radius $= 4.25 - 0.05 = 4.20$ cm and height $= 1.0 - 0.05 = 0.95$ cm
Volume of the cavity $= \pi (4.20)^2 (0.95) = 52.647$ cm$^3$
Plastic in the cylindrical base $= 56.745 - 52.647 = 4.098$ cm$^3$
Add the trapezoidal prism opening, whose volume is given as $0.33$ cm$^3$, and subtract the sip opening cut through the $0.05$ cm top face (footprint $2.5$ cm by $2.0$ cm at the base, so approximately $0.21$ cm$^3$):
Volume of a new lid $= 4.098 + 0.33 - 0.21$
$= 4.2192$
$\approx 4.22$ cm$^3$

parts.text: Starbucks plastic lids are made from polypropylene, a type of plastic with density $0.92$ g/cm$^3$. Density is given by the formula density $= \frac{\text{mass}}{\text{volume}}$, where mass is measured in grams and volume in cm$^3$. The mass of the common plastic lid and straw combo is estimated to be $3.55$ g. Comparing the new lid with the common plastic lid and straw combo, which option is better? Explain and justify your answer with calculations.
parts.label: b
parts.answer: Mass of a new lid $= 0.92 \times 4.2192 = 3.88$ g, which is $0.33$ g heavier than the $3.55$ g combo. Either conclusion is accepted with justification: the lid and straw combo is better because it uses less plastic by mass, or the new lid is better because it is recyclable while the straw is not.
parts.solution:
From the density formula, mass $=$ density $\times$ volume.
Mass of a new lid $= 0.92 \times 4.2192$
$= 3.881664$ g
Mass of the plastic lid and straw combo $= 3.55$ g
Difference $= 3.881664 - 3.55 = 0.331664$ g
So each new lid is about $0.33$ g heavier than the lid and straw combo.
Either justified conclusion is accepted:
The plastic lid and straw combo is better, because it has the smaller mass and so uses less plastic per drink.
OR the new lid is better, because although it is $0.33$ g heavier it is recyclable, whereas the straw is too small and light to be recycled and ends up in landfills and waterways.

stem: **In this question, you should state the parameters of any distributions you use.**

parts.text:
The number of hours worked per week by employees of Company $A$ follow a normal distribution with mean 40 hours and standard deviation $\alpha$ hours, while the number of hours worked per week by employees of Company $B$ follow a normal distribution with mean 40 hours and standard deviation $\beta$ hours, where $\alpha > \beta$.
The diagram shows the probability density function of $X$, where $X$ is the random variable denoting the number of hours worked per week by a randomly chosen employee of Company $A$.
parts.label: a

subparts.text: On the copy of the diagram in the **Printed Answer Booklet**, sketch on the same diagram the probability density function of $Y$, where $Y$ is the random variable denoting the number of hours worked per week by a randomly chosen employee of Company $B$.
subparts.label: i
subparts.solution: [See solution diagram - normal distribution curve centered at 40, with $X$ and $Y$ axes labeled]

subparts.text:
The probability that a randomly chosen employee of Company $A$ works less than $t$ hours per week is represented by the shaded area of the standard normal curve in the diagram below.

Write down an equation involving $t$ and $\alpha$.
subparts.label: ii

subparts.text: Two employees of company $A$ are randomly chosen. Find the probability that both employees work more than $t$ hours per week.
subparts.label: iii

subparts.text: Given that the probability that a randomly chosen employee of Company $B$ works more than 42 hours per week is at least 0.25 , find the range of values of $\beta$.
subparts.label: iv
subparts.solution:
$Y \sim N(40, \beta^2)$
$P(Y > 42) \geq 0.25$
$P\left(\frac{Y-40}{\beta} > \frac{2}{\beta}\right) \geq 0.25$
$P\left(Z > \frac{2}{\beta}\right) \geq 0.25$
$\frac{2}{\beta} \leq 0.67449$
$\beta \geq 2.9652 = 2.97$

parts.text: A shop sells small and large bags of rice. The masses of small bags of rice are normally distributed with mean 1 kg and standard deviation 0.16 kg . The masses of large bags of rice have mean 5 kg and standard deviation 0.5 kg . The masses of the small and large bags of rice are independent of one another.
parts.label: b

subparts.text: In a random sample of 300 small bags of rice, find the expected number of bags that have a mass greater than 1.25 kg .
subparts.label: i
subparts.solution:
Let $S$ be the mass, in kg, of a small bag of rice.
$S \sim N(1, 0.16^2)$
$P(S > 1.25) = 0.059085$
Let $W$ be the number of small bags with mass greater than 1.25 kg out of 300 bags.
$W \sim B(300, 0.059085)$
$E(W) = 300 \times 0.059085 = 17.7$
Expected number of small bags of rice with a mass greater than 1.25 kg is 17.7.

subparts.text: Find the probability that the total mass of 5 randomly chosen small bags of rice exceed the mean mass of 30 randomly chosen large bags of rice by more than 0.25 kg .
subparts.label: ii
subparts.solution:
Let $L$ be the mass, in kg, of a big bag of rice.
Since $n = 30$ is large enough, by Central Limit Theorem,
$\bar{L} \sim N\left(5, \frac{0.5^2}{30}\right)$ approximately.
Let $W = S_1 + S_2 + \cdots + S_5 - \bar{L}$.
$E(W) = 5E(S) - E(\bar{L}) = 5(1) - 5 = 0$
$\text{Var}(W) = 5\text{Var}(S) + \text{Var}(\bar{L}) = 5(0.16^2) + \frac{0.5^2}{30} = \frac{409}{3000}$
$\therefore W \sim N\left(0, \frac{409}{3000}\right)$ approximately.
Required Prob. $= P(W > 0.25) = 0.249$ (3 s.f.)

stem: A vase that is 17 cm tall can be modelled by a frustum, $A$, on top of an egg-shaped container, $B$. A sketch of the vase is shown in Figure 1. Figure 2 shows the cone that the frustum $A$ is a part of. The diameter $QRS$ of the top of the frustum is $8$ cm and the diameter $PVT$ of the bottom is $7$ cm. The height of the frustum, $RV$, is $8$ cm. $R$ and $V$ are the midpoints of $QS$ and $PT$ respectively.

parts.text: Calculate the volume of the frustum, $A$.
parts.label: a
parts.solution:
Let $UV = x$ cm. Triangles $UPT$ and $UQS$ are similar.
$\dfrac{x}{7} = \dfrac{x + 8}{8}$
$8x = 7x + 56$
$x = 56$
$UR = 56 + 8 = 64$ cm
Volume of $A = \dfrac{1}{3}\pi \left(\dfrac{8}{2}\right)^{2}(64) - \dfrac{1}{3}\pi \left(\dfrac{7}{2}\right)^{2}(56)$
$= 353.9528$
$\approx 354\ \text{cm}^{3}\ (3\text{ s.f.})$

parts.text: The volume of $B$ is about $650\ \text{cm}^{3}$ and its height is $9$ cm. Water is poured into the vase at the rate of $10\ \text{cm}^{3}$ per second until it is full. Sketch the height of the water in the vase with respect to time.
parts.label: b
parts.answer: Curve starting at origin, concave (steep then slower) for egg-shaped portion from $t = 0$ to about $t = 65$ s reaching height $9$ cm, then increasing more gently (widening frustum) up to $17$ cm at about $t = 100$ s.
parts.solution:
Time to fill $B$: $\dfrac{650}{10} = 65$ s, with water reaching height $9$ cm.
Time to fill $A$: $\dfrac{354}{10} \approx 35.4$ s additional, total $\approx 100.4$ s.
Total height $= 17$ cm.
Sketch: $(0, 0)$ rising rapidly initially through the egg shape (concave shape due to widening then narrowing of the egg), passes through approximately $(65, 9)$, then continues to rise more gradually through the widening frustum, ending at approximately $(100.4, 17)$.

stem: Retrieved from The Straits Times, 10 June 2023. More budget meal options are in the works for Singaporeans. The Housing Board, in collaboration with the Government Technology Agency, launched the BudgetMealGoWhere website to help residents locate HDB coffee shops offering budget meals within $2$ km of their residence. parts.text:
After meeting Mary, Sally needs to run multiple errands to different parts of Singapore. She decides to rent a car from 8am to 12pm for that day. The tables showing the cost of car rental from two companies, GetCar and FindCar, are given in the diagram above. The table below shows the price per litre of different grades of petrol from three different petrol companies, Company Messo, Company Shore and Company SCP. Each litre of petrol allows $12.5$ km of travel.
$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|} \hline \text{Petrol Grade} & \text{Company Messo} & \text{Company Shore} & \text{Company SCP} \\ \hline  & \text{Price per litre (discounted price with ABC Bank credit card)} & & \\ \hline 92 & \$2.70 \text{ (NA)} & - & \$2.70 \text{ (NA)} \\ \hline 95 & \$2.75 \text{ (NA)} & \$2.79 \text{ (\$2.20)} & \$2.74 \text{ (NA)} \\ \hline 98 & \$3.22 \text{ (NA)} & \$3.28 \text{ (\$2.59)} & \$3.22 \text{ (NA)} \\ \hline \end{array}$$
Sally estimates that she needs to travel $67$ km that day. She carries an ABC Bank credit card. She wants to minimise her costs in the rental. Suggest the company from which Sally should rent the car. Justify any decisions you make and show your calculations clearly.
parts.label: b
parts.answer:
Sally should rent from GetCar.
GetCar: rental $= \$7 \times 4 = \$28$; mileage $= \$0.39 \times 67 = \$26.13$; total $= \$54.13$.
FindCar: rental $= \$3 + \$5 \times 3 = \$18$; mileage $= \$0.39 \times 67 = \$26.13$; petrol needed $= 67/12.5 = 5.36$ L at \$2.20 per litre $= \$11.79$; total $= \$18 + \$26.13 + \$11.79 = \$55.92$.
Since $\$54.13 < \$55.92$, Sally should rent from GetCar.
parts.solution:
Renting from GetCar:
Car rental & mileage charges $= (\$7 \times 4) + (\$0.39 \times 67)$
$= \$54.13$

Renting from FindCar:
Car rental & mileage charges $= (\$3 \times 1 + \$5 \times 3) + (\$0.39 \times 67)$
$= \$44.13$

Amount of petrol needed $= \dfrac{67}{12.5} = 5.36$ litres

Fuel charges $= \$2.20 \times 5.36 = \$11.792$

Total charges (FindCar) $= 44.13 + 11.792 = \$55.92 > \$54.13$

Since it costs less to rent from GetCar, Sally should rent from Company GetCar.

stem: $ABCD$ is a trapezium with an area of $88\text{ cm}^{2}$.

parts.text: Show that the height of the trapezium is 8 cm.
parts.label: a
parts.solution:

stem: The diagram shows the positions of four checkpoints $W$, $X$, $Y$ and $Z$ in a jungle reserve area. The checkpoints are connected by the irregular tracks shown. $X$ is due north of $Y$ and is on a bearing of $077^{\circ}$ from $W$. Angle $XWY = 53^{\circ}$ and $WY$ is $60$ metres.

parts.text: Calculate the distance $XY$.
parts.label: i
parts.solution:
Since $X$ is due north of $Y$, the bearing of $W$ from $X$ is $077^{\circ} + 180^{\circ} = 257^{\circ}$, and $XY$ points due south ($180^{\circ}$) from $X$.
$\angle WXY = 257^{\circ} - 180^{\circ} = 77^{\circ}$.
$\angle WYX = 180^{\circ} - 53^{\circ} - 77^{\circ} = 50^{\circ}$.
By the sine rule: $\dfrac{XY}{\sin \angle XWY} = \dfrac{WY}{\sin \angle WXY}$
$XY = \dfrac{60 \sin 53^{\circ}}{\sin 77^{\circ}} = 49.18$ m

parts.text: Given that the bearing of $Y$ from $Z$ is $152^{\circ}$, write down the bearing of $Z$ from $Y$.
parts.label: ii
parts.solution: Bearing of $Z$ from $Y = $ bearing of $Y$ from $Z$ $+ 180^{\circ} = 152^{\circ} + 180^{\circ} = 332^{\circ}$.

parts.text: A hidden camera, $C$, is to be fixed at checkpoint $Y$ to capture animals that move from $W$ to $Y$ via $Z$, along the irregular track. The camera has a view angle of $50^{\circ}$ and can capture anything within this angle, as shown in the diagram below. By measurement, determine the minimum bearing where the line $CP$ must be pointed when the camera is fixed at point $Y$.
parts.label: iii
parts.solution:
The camera at $Y$ has a $50^{\circ}$ field of view that must cover the track from $W$ to $Y$ via $Z$.
From the scale diagram, the line $CP$ must be pointed at a minimum bearing of approximately $281^{\circ}$ to $283^{\circ}$ so that the whole track lies within the $50^{\circ}$ view angle.
