Median: every recorded value is $1$ hour too high, so the actual median decreases by $1$ hour, from $34$ h to $33$ h.
Standard deviation: subtracting the same amount from every value does not change the spread, so the standard deviation remains the same.

stem: The diagram shows a cuboid of length $30$ cm. The width of the cuboid is $x$ cm. The height of the cuboid is $y$ cm. The surface area of the cuboid is $1200$ cm$^{2}$.

parts.text: Find an expression, in terms of $x$, for $y$.
parts.label: a

parts.text: Show that the volume of the cuboid, $V$ cm$^{3}$, is given by $V = \dfrac{18000x - 900x^{2}}{x + 30}$.
parts.label: b
parts.solution:
Volume $= 30xy = 30x\left(\dfrac{600 - 30x}{x + 30}\right)$
$= \dfrac{18000x - 900x^{2}}{x + 30}$ (shown)

parts.text:
Complete the table of values for $V = \dfrac{18000x - 900x^{2}}{x + 30}$. Values are given to the nearest whole number.
$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|} \hline x & 4 & 6 & 8 & 10 & 12 & 14 & 15 \\ \hline V & 1694 & 2100 & & 2250 & 2057 & 1718 & 1500 \\ \hline \end{array}$$
parts.label: c

parts.text: On the grid, draw the graph of $V = \dfrac{18000x - 900x^{2}}{x + 30}$ for $4 \leq x \leq 15$.
parts.label: d
parts.answer: Smooth curve through the table values, rising from $x = 4$ to a maximum between $x = 8$ and $x = 10$, then falling to $1500$ at $x = 15$.
parts.solution: A smooth curve is drawn through the plotted points $(4, 1694)$, $(6, 2100)$, $(8, 2274)$, $(10, 2250)$, $(12, 2057)$, $(14, 1718)$, $(15, 1500)$, rising to a maximum between $x = 8$ and $x = 10$ then falling.

parts.text: Use your graph to find the greatest value of $x$ when the volume is equal to $2000$ cm$^{3}$.
parts.label: e
parts.solution: From the graph, when $V = 2000$, the greatest value of $x = 12.4 \pm 0.2$.

parts.text: Explain how the graph shows that there is no solution to the equation $$18000x - 900x^{2} = 2400x + 72000.$$
parts.label: f
parts.answer: Dividing both sides by $(x + 30)$ gives $V = 2400$. The greatest value of $V$ on the graph is about $2274$, so the horizontal line $V = 2400$ lies entirely above the curve for $4 \leq x \leq 15$, hence there is no intersection and no solution in this range.
parts.solution:
$18000x - 900x^{2} = 2400x + 72000$
$18000x - 900x^{2} = 2400(x + 30)$
$\dfrac{18000x - 900x^{2}}{x + 30} = 2400$, i.e. $V = 2400$.
The greatest value of $V$ on the graph is about $2290$, so the line $V = 2400$ lies entirely above the curve for $4 \leq x \leq 15$.
Hence there is no intersection, so the equation has no solution in this range.

stem: Fig. 1 shows the top view of a narrow corridor of width 1.2 units which leads into a wide linkway of width 9.6 units. The distance measured from a point $A$ of the corridor to a point $B$ of the wall of the linkway opposite the corridor is $x$ units as shown in the diagram, where $A$ and $B$ are at the same height above the ground, which is assumed to be level. $AB$ touches the edge of the corridor at point $E$, making an angle $\theta$, where $0 < \theta < \frac{\pi}{2}$, with the wall of the linkway.

parts.text: Show that $x = 1.2\sec\theta + 9.6\csc\theta$.
parts.label: a
parts.solution:
$\cos\theta = \frac{1.2}{AE} \Rightarrow AE = \frac{1.2}{\cos\theta}$
$\sin\theta = \frac{9.6}{BE} \Rightarrow BE = \frac{9.6}{\sin\theta}$
$x = AE + BE = \frac{1.2}{\cos\theta} + \frac{9.6}{\sin\theta} = 1.2\sec\theta + 9.6\csc\theta$ (shown)

parts.text: A renovation worker needs to carry a long metal rod horizontally from point $P$ to point $Q$. Using differentiation, find the exact length of the longest rod, of negligible thickness, that the renovation worker can carry horizontally from $P$ to $Q$.
parts.label: b
parts.solution:
$x = 1.2\sec\theta + 9.6\csc\theta$
$\frac{dx}{d\theta} = 1.2\sec\theta\tan\theta - 9.6\csc\theta\cot\theta$
When $\frac{dx}{d\theta} = 0$:
$1.2\sec\theta\tan\theta = 9.6\csc\theta\cot\theta$
$\left(\frac{1}{\cos\theta}\right)\left(\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}\right) = 8\left(\frac{1}{\sin\theta}\right)\left(\frac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}\right)$
$\sin^3\theta = 8\cos^3\theta$
$\tan^3\theta = 8 \Rightarrow \tan\theta = 2$
$\frac{d^2x}{d\theta^2} = 1.2\left(\sec\theta\tan^2\theta + \sec^3\theta\right) + 9.6\left(\csc\theta\cot^2\theta + \csc^3\theta\right)$
At $\theta = \tan^{-1} 2$: $\frac{d^2x}{d\theta^2} = 40.2 > 0$ (3 s.f.), so $x$ is a minimum.
The minimum $x$ is the minimum distance between the two walls, which corresponds to the maximum length of thin rod that can be carried horizontally.
Since $\tan\theta = 2$: $\sin\theta = \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}$ and $\cos\theta = \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}$.
Length of longest rod $= 1.2\sec\theta + 9.6\csc\theta = 1.2\sqrt{5} + 9.6\left(\frac{\sqrt{5}}{2}\right) = 6\sqrt{5}$ units.

parts.text: If the narrow corridor leads into a rectangular room with dimension 15 units by 9.6 units, in the middle of one side of the room instead (see Fig. 2), find the length of the longest rod, of negligible thickness, that the renovation worker can now carry horizontally from $P$ into the room.
parts.label: c
parts.solution:
$l = 6.9 + 1.2 = 8.1$
From the diagram, $L = \sqrt{8.1^2 + 9.6^2} = \sqrt{157.77} = 12.6$ units (3 s.f.).
Since $L$ is shorter than the $6\sqrt{5}$ found in (b), the length of the longest rod that can be carried into this room is $12.6$ units.

parts.text: Charles needs to take a certification test to become a physical instructor. He takes the test until he passes. Each time he takes the test, the probability that Charles passes is $0.8$. Find the probability that Charles
parts.label: d

subparts.text: passes only at the third attempt,
subparts.label: i
subparts.solution:
P(Charles fails) $= 1 - 0.8 = 0.2$
P(Charles passes only at the third attempt) $= 0.2 \times 0.2 \times 0.8 = 0.032$

stem: The diagram shows a solid consisting of a right circular cone attached to a hemisphere with a common base which is a circle of radius $6$ cm. The volume of the cone is equal to twice the volume of the hemisphere.

parts.text: Show that the height of the cone is $24$ cm.
parts.label: a
parts.solution:
Let the height of the cone be $h$.
Volume of cone $= 2 \times$ Volume of hemisphere
$\dfrac{1}{3}\pi(6)^2 h = 2 \times \dfrac{2}{3}\pi(6)^3$
$12h = 288$
$h = \dfrac{288}{12}$
$h = 24$ cm (shown)

parts.text: Find the total surface area of the solid.
parts.label: b
parts.solution:
Let the slant height of the cone be $l$.
By Pythagoras' Theorem,
$l^2 = 6^2 + 24^2$
$l = \sqrt{612}$
$l = 24.739$ (5 s.f.)
Total surface area of solid $= \pi(6)(24.739) + 2\pi(6)^2$
$= 692.51$ cm$^2$
$= 693$ cm$^2$ (3 s.f.)

parts.text: The same solid is cut into two parts such that the upper part is a cone of base radius $x$ cm and height $y$ cm.
parts.label: c

subparts.text: Find the value of $\dfrac{x}{y}$.
subparts.label: i
subparts.solution: $\dfrac{x}{y} = \dfrac{6}{24} = \dfrac{1}{4}$ (by similar triangles)

subparts.text: Find the value of $y$ such that the volume of the upper part is equal to the volume of the lower part.
subparts.label: ii
subparts.solution:
$\dfrac{x}{y} = \dfrac{1}{4}$, so $x = \dfrac{1}{4}y$.
Volume of frustum $= \dfrac{1}{3}\pi(6)^2(24) - \dfrac{1}{3}\pi x^2 y$
Volume of upper cone $=$ Volume of frustum $+$ Volume of hemisphere
$\dfrac{1}{3}\pi x^2 y = \dfrac{1}{3}\pi(6)^2(24) - \dfrac{1}{3}\pi x^2 y + \dfrac{2}{3}\pi(6)^3$
$\dfrac{2}{3}\pi x^2 y = \dfrac{1}{3}\pi(6)^2(24) + \dfrac{2}{3}\pi(6)^3$
$\dfrac{2}{3}x^2 y = \dfrac{1}{3}(6)^2(24) + \dfrac{2}{3}(6)^3$ (divide both sides by $\pi$)
$\dfrac{2}{3}x^2 y = 432$
Sub $x = \dfrac{1}{4}y$ into the equation,
$\dfrac{2}{3}\left(\dfrac{1}{4}y\right)^2 y = 432$
$\dfrac{1}{24}y^3 = 432$
$y^3 = 10368$
$y = 21.8$ cm (3 s.f.)

stem: It is given that the volume of a circular cone with base radius $r$ and vertical height $h$ is $\frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h$.

parts.text: A hopper consists of an open cylinder of height $h$ m joined to an open cone of radius $r$ m and height $h$ m (see Fig. 1). The slant edge of the cone has a fixed length of $2$ m. As $r$ and $h$ vary, use differentiation to find the exact maximum volume of the hopper.
parts.label: i
parts.solution:
Slant edge $= 2$: $h^2 + r^2 = 2^2$, so $r^2 = 4 - h^2$.
Volume of hopper $= $ cylinder $+$ cone $= \pi r^2 h + \dfrac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^2 h$.
$V = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi h(4 - h^2) = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi(4h - h^3)$
$\dfrac{dV}{dh} = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi(4 - 3h^2)$
At stationary values, $4 - 3h^2 = 0 \Rightarrow h = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}$ (since $h > 0$).
$\dfrac{d^2V}{dh^2} = -8\pi h < 0$, so $V$ is a maximum.
Maximum volume $V = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi\left(\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\right)\left(\dfrac{8}{3}\right) = \dfrac{64}{9\sqrt{3}}\pi$ m$^3$.

parts.text: A coffee manufacturer uses such a hopper that has a cone of radius $1.2$ m. For each batch, the coffee drink is initially filled to the brim of the hopper and mixed thoroughly before it is transferred to the packing chamber at a constant rate of $0.2$ m$^3$/s. At a particular point in time, the height of the coffee drink in the cylindrical section is $2.4$ m from the bottom of the cone (see Fig. 2, shaded region). Find the rate at which the height of the coffee drink is changing at this instant.
parts.label: ii
parts.solution:
Coffee leaves at a constant rate, so $\dfrac{dV}{dt} = -0.2$ m$^3$/s. The surface is in the cylindrical section, radius constant at $1.2$ m.
For the cylinder, $V = \pi(1.2)^2 H$, so $\dfrac{dV}{dt} = \pi(1.2)^2\dfrac{dH}{dt}$.
$\dfrac{dH}{dt} = \dfrac{-0.2}{\pi(1.2)^2} = -0.0442$ m/s.
The height is decreasing at $0.0442$ m/s.

parts.text: After some time has passed in the transfer process, there remains some coffee drink in the conical section with radius $p$ m and height $q$ m (see Fig. 3, shaded region). Find $p$ in terms of $q$ and hence calculate the rate of decrease of $q$ when $q = 0.5$.
parts.label: iii
parts.solution:
Height of the full cone $= \sqrt{4 - 1.2^2} = 1.6$ m.
By similar triangles, $\dfrac{p}{q} = \dfrac{1.2}{1.6}$, so $p = \dfrac{3q}{4}$.
Volume remaining in the cone: $V_2 = \dfrac{1}{3}\pi p^2 q = \dfrac{1}{3}\pi\left(\dfrac{3q}{4}\right)^2 q = \dfrac{3}{16}\pi q^3$.
$\dfrac{dV_2}{dq} = \dfrac{9}{16}\pi q^2$
Using $\dfrac{dV_2}{dt} = \dfrac{dV_2}{dq}\cdot\dfrac{dq}{dt}$ with $\dfrac{dV_2}{dt} = -0.2$, $q = 0.5$:
$-0.2 = \dfrac{9}{16}\pi(0.5)^2\dfrac{dq}{dt}$
$\dfrac{dq}{dt} = -0.453$
$q$ is decreasing at $0.453$ m/s.

stem: An equilateral triangle $ABC$ has sides of 8 cm. $O$ is the centre of the equilateral triangle.

parts.text: Show that the length of $OA$ is $4.619$ cm, correct to 3 decimal places.

parts.solution:
$\angle AOB = 120^\circ$, $\angle ABO = 30^\circ$
$\dfrac{OA}{\sin 30^\circ} = \dfrac{8}{\sin 120^\circ}$
$OA = \dfrac{8}{\sin 120^\circ}\times\sin 30^\circ \approx 4.6188$ cm
$= 4.619$ cm (3 d.p.)

parts.text: The triangle $ABC$ forms the base of a pyramid. The vertex $X$ is vertically above $O$ and $AX=18$ cm. Calculate the total surface area of the pyramid.

Base area $\triangle ABC = \dfrac{1}{2}(8)(8)\sin 60^\circ \approx 27.7128$ cm$^2$
Slant height of $\triangle AXB$, $l = \sqrt{18^{2}-4^{2}} \approx 17.5499$ cm
Total surface area $= 3\times\dfrac{1}{2}(8)(17.5499)+27.7128$
$\approx 238.31$ cm$^2 = 238$ cm$^2$ (3 s.f.)

parts.text:

Key: Each circle represents $20$ students.

stem: A manufacturer designs a cylindrical water dispenser with a fixed volume, $V$ cm$^{3}$ where $V > 1$. The manufacturer decides to use stainless steel, with negligible thickness, for the cylindrical body of the water dispenser of height $y$ cm and the circular base of radius $r$ cm. Plastic, with negligible thickness, will be used instead for the circular lid of radius $r$ cm, as shown in Diagram 1. In order to insert a tap, an area of $1$ cm$^{2}$ of stainless steel will be removed from the cylindrical body of the water dispenser. The total area of stainless steel to be used for the cylindrical body and circular base of the water dispenser, as shown in Diagram 2, is denoted by $A$ cm$^{2}$. The manufacturer wants the value of $A$ to be as small as possible.

parts.text: Show that $A = \pi r^{2} + \frac{2V}{r} - 1$.
parts.label: i
parts.solution:
$V = \pi r^2 y$
$y = \frac{V}{\pi r^2}$ ... (1)
$A = \pi r^2 + 2\pi r y - 1$ ... (2)
Substitute (1) into (2):
$A = \pi r^2 + 2\pi r\left(\frac{V}{\pi r^2}\right) - 1$
$A = \pi r^2 + \frac{2V}{r} - 1$ (Shown)

parts.text: Using differentiation, find in terms of $V$ and $\pi$, the minimum value of $A$, proving that it is a minimum. Simplify your answer.
parts.label: ii
parts.solution:
$\frac{dA}{dr} = 2\pi r - \frac{2V}{r^2}$
When $\frac{dA}{dr} = 0$:
$2\pi r = \frac{2V}{r^2} \Rightarrow r^3 = \frac{V}{\pi} \Rightarrow r = \sqrt[3]{\frac{V}{\pi}}$
$\frac{d^2A}{dr^2} = 2\pi + \frac{4V}{r^3}$
When $r = \sqrt[3]{\frac{V}{\pi}}$: $\frac{d^2A}{dr^2} = 2\pi + \frac{4V}{\frac{V}{\pi}} = 2\pi + 4\pi = 6\pi > 0$
Therefore $A$ is minimum when $r = \sqrt[3]{\frac{V}{\pi}}$.
Minimum value of $A$:
$= \pi\left(\sqrt[3]{\frac{V}{\pi}}\right)^2 + \frac{2V}{\sqrt[3]{\frac{V}{\pi}}} - 1$
$= \frac{\pi\left(\sqrt[3]{\frac{V}{\pi}}\right)^3 + 2V}{\sqrt[3]{\frac{V}{\pi}}} - 1$
$= \frac{V + 2V}{\sqrt[3]{\frac{V}{\pi}}} - 1$
$= \frac{3V}{\sqrt[3]{\frac{V}{\pi}}} - 1$
$= 3(V^2\pi)^{\frac{1}{3}} - 1$

parts.text: Sketch the graph of $A$ as $r$ varies, stating the coordinates of any turning point(s) in terms of $V$ and $\pi$ and the equations of any asymptotes.
parts.label: iii
parts.solution:
The graph of $A$ against $r$ has a minimum turning point at $\left(\left(\frac{V}{\pi}\right)^{\frac{1}{3}},\ 3(V^2\pi)^{\frac{1}{3}} - 1\right)$ and a vertical asymptote $r = 0$.
See sketch.

parts.text: It is given that the water dispenser, with the minimum value of $A$ found in part (ii), is completely filled with water. When the tap is turned on, the rate of decrease of the volume of water, $W$ cm$^{3}$, in the water dispenser with respect to time $t$ seconds is $ye^{-\frac{t}{\pi r^{3}}}$ cm$^{3}$/s. Find the rate of change of the height of water, $h$ cm, in the water dispenser 1 minute after the tap is turned on, as shown in Diagram 3. Simplify your answer in terms of $V$ and $\pi$.
parts.label: iv
parts.solution:
$W = \pi r^2 h$ is the volume of water and $h$ cm is the height of water.
Given $\frac{dW}{dt} = -y\,e^{-\frac{t}{\pi r^3}}$.
When $A$ is minimum, $r = \sqrt[3]{\frac{V}{\pi}}$ and $y = \frac{V}{\pi r^2} = \frac{V}{\pi\left(\sqrt[3]{\frac{V}{\pi}}\right)^2} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{V}{\pi}}$.
Therefore $W = \pi\left(\sqrt[3]{\frac{V}{\pi}}\right)^2 h \Rightarrow W = (V^2\pi)^{\frac{1}{3}} h$
$\frac{dW}{dh} = (V^2\pi)^{\frac{1}{3}}$
$\frac{dh}{dt} = \frac{dh}{dW} \times \frac{dW}{dt} = \frac{1}{(V^2\pi)^{\frac{1}{3}}} \times \left(-y\,e^{-\frac{t}{\pi r^3}}\right)$
When $t = 1$ min $= 60$ s, with $r = \sqrt[3]{\frac{V}{\pi}}$ (so $\pi r^3 = V$) and $y = \sqrt[3]{\frac{V}{\pi}}$:
$\frac{dh}{dt} = -\frac{\sqrt[3]{\frac{V}{\pi}}\,e^{-\frac{60}{V}}}{(V^2\pi)^{\frac{1}{3}}} = -\frac{e^{-\frac{60}{V}}}{(\pi^2 V)^{\frac{1}{3}}}$ cm/s
The rate of change of the height of water is decreasing.

stem: The stem-and-leaf diagram shows the time, in seconds, taken by some students to complete a task.

parts.text: Find the range.
parts.label: a
parts.solution:
Range $=$ largest value $-$ smallest value
$= 114 - 40 = 74$ s

parts.text: Find the median.
parts.label: b
parts.solution:
There are $23$ values, so the median is the $12^{\text{th}}$ value when they are in order.
Counting through the stem-and-leaf diagram gives
Median $= 73$ s

parts.text: Construct a box-and-whisker plot that represents the above data. Label the crucial data clearly.
parts.label: c
parts.answer: Box-and-whisker plot with minimum $= 40$, lower quartile $= 64$, median $= 73$, upper quartile $= 84$, maximum $= 114$.
parts.solution:
The five values needed are read from the ordered data:
minimum $= 40$, lower quartile $= 64$, median $= 73$, upper quartile $= 84$, maximum $= 114$.
Draw a box from $64$ to $84$ with a line at $73$, and whiskers out to $40$ and $114$, all against a numbered time axis.

parts.text: The students are expected to take at most $70$ seconds to complete the task. Find, as a fraction in its simplest form, the probability that
parts.label: d

subparts.text: a student, who is randomly selected, meets the expectation of the teacher,
subparts.label: i
subparts.solution:
$10$ of the $23$ students meet the expectation.
$P = \dfrac{10}{23}$

subparts.text: one of the two students who are randomly selected, does not meet the expectation of the teacher.
subparts.label: ii
subparts.solution:
$13$ of the $23$ do not meet the expectation.
Exactly one of the two selected does not meet it — the other one does — and this can happen in two orders:
$P = \dfrac{13}{23} \times \dfrac{10}{22} + \dfrac{10}{23} \times \dfrac{13}{22}$
$= 2 \times \dfrac{130}{506} = \dfrac{260}{506} = \dfrac{130}{253}$

stem: Daredevil is performing a motorcycle stunt where he drives himself off from one inclined platform on the left (L) to land safely on a platform on the right (R). His motion in the air can be modelled by the quadratic equation $y = -\frac{1}{2}x^2 + x + 6$, where his vertical height from the ground is $y$ units and his horizontal position is $x$ units. The left platform (L), which is marked with a cross on the photograph, is situated at horizontal position $x = -2$. The graph of $y = -\frac{1}{2}x^2 + x + 6$ for $-2 \leq x \leq 4$ is given on the grid below. Using the graph given, answer the following:

parts.text: Find the height of the left platform (L).
parts.label: a
parts.solution:
The left platform is at $x = -2$. From the graph, when $x = -2$, $y = 2$.
Check: $y = -\frac{1}{2}(-2)^2 + (-2) + 6 = -2 - 2 + 6 = 2$.
The height of the left platform is 2 units.

parts.text: If the landing platform is 3.1 units high, find the distance between the two platforms for Daredevil to land safely right at the edge of the landing platform.
parts.label: b
parts.solution:
From the graph, draw the line $y = 3.1$ and read off the $x$-value on the descending branch: $x \approx 3.6$.
Check: $-\frac{1}{2}x^2 + x + 6 = 3.1$ gives $x^2 - 2x - 5.8 = 0$, so $x = 3.607\ldots$
$$\text{Distance} = 3.6 - (-2) = 5.6 \text{ units}$$

parts.text: Write down the equation of the line of symmetry of his motion.
parts.label: c
parts.solution:
From the graph the curve is symmetrical about the vertical line through the maximum point at $x = 1$.
$$x = 1$$

parts.text: Find
parts.label: d

subparts.text: the maximum vertical distance attained by Daredevil as measured from the ground, and
subparts.label: i
subparts.solution:
From the graph the highest point of the curve is at $(1,\ 6.5)$.
The maximum vertical distance from the ground is $6.5$ units.

subparts.text: the horizontal distance from the left platform (L) at this position, where the vertical distance is maximum.
subparts.label: ii
subparts.solution:
The maximum occurs at $x = 1$ and the left platform is at $x = -2$.
$$\text{Horizontal distance} = 1 - (-2) = 3 \text{ units}$$

parts.text: Daredevil performed the stunt a second time, but his motion is then modelled by another quadratic equation $y = -x^2 + x + 8$. By drawing a suitable linear graph on the same diagram, find the horizontal distance(s) travelled by Daredevil when he is at a height of 4 units above his starting position on the left platform (L).
parts.label: e
parts.answer: Draw the line $y = \frac{1}{2}x + 5$; the horizontal distances are 1 unit and 4 units.
parts.solution:
On the second attempt the starting height at $x = -2$ is $y = -(-2)^2 + (-2) + 8 = 2$ units, so a height of 4 units above the starting position means $y = 2 + 4 = 6$.
Required: $-x^2 + x + 8 = 6$, i.e. $-x^2 + x + 2 = 0$.
Halve it: $-\frac{1}{2}x^2 + \frac{1}{2}x + 1 = 0$.
Add $\frac{1}{2}x + 5$ to both sides so that the left side becomes the plotted curve:
$$-\frac{1}{2}x^2 + x + 6 = \frac{1}{2}x + 5$$
So draw the straight line $y = \frac{1}{2}x + 5$ on the same axes (it passes through $(-2,\ 4)$ and $(4,\ 7)$).
The line cuts the curve at $x = -1$ and $x = 2$.
Horizontal distances from L at $x = -2$:
$$-1 - (-2) = 1 \text{ unit} \quad \text{and} \quad 2 - (-2) = 4 \text{ units}$$

stem: Figure 1 shows a rectangular swimming pool and Figure 2 represents the cross-sectional view of the pool. The pool is $\left(x^2 + x\right)$ m long, $\left(\frac{x^2 + x - 6}{x + 1}\right)$ m wide and $\left(\frac{1}{x - 2}\right)$ m deep. The shaded region shows the base of the pool which is made of concrete. Find, as a single fraction in terms of $x$, the simplified expression of

parts.text: the height of the concrete, $y$, in metres, used for the base of the pool,
parts.label: a
parts.solution:
From Figure 2, the depth of the pool is made up of the water depth $\frac{5}{x^2 + x - 6}$ and the concrete height $y$:
$$y = \frac{1}{x - 2} - \frac{5}{x^2 + x - 6}$$
$$x^2 + x - 6 = (x + 3)(x - 2)$$
$$y = \frac{1}{x - 2} - \frac{5}{(x + 3)(x - 2)} = \frac{(x + 3) - 5}{(x + 3)(x - 2)} = \frac{x - 2}{(x + 3)(x - 2)}$$
$$y = \frac{1}{x + 3}$$

parts.text: the cross-sectional area of the concrete used for the base of the pool,
parts.label: b
parts.solution:
The shaded concrete is a trapezium with parallel sides $\left(x^2 + x\right)$ m and $3(x + 1)$ m, and height $y$ m.
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2}\left[\left(x^2 + x\right) + 3(x + 1)\right] \times \frac{1}{x + 3}$$
$$= \frac{1}{2}\left(x^2 + 4x + 3\right) \times \frac{1}{x + 3} = \frac{(x + 1)(x + 3)}{2(x + 3)}$$
$$= \frac{x + 1}{2} \text{ m}^2$$

parts.text: the volume of water needed to fill the pool completely, by using your answer obtained in part (b).
parts.label: c
parts.solution:
Total cross-sectional area of the pool
$$= \left(x^2 + x\right) \times \frac{1}{x - 2} = \frac{x(x + 1)}{x - 2}$$
Cross-sectional area of the water
$$= \frac{x(x + 1)}{x - 2} - \frac{x + 1}{2} = (x + 1)\left[\frac{2x - (x - 2)}{2(x - 2)}\right] = \frac{(x + 1)(x + 2)}{2(x - 2)}$$
Volume of water $=$ cross-sectional area $\times$ width
$$= \frac{(x + 1)(x + 2)}{2(x - 2)} \times \frac{(x + 3)(x - 2)}{x + 1} = \frac{(x + 2)(x + 3)}{2} \text{ m}^3$$

stem: Singapore aims to be a test-bed for micro-wind technology generating electricity with low wind speeds. A wind power station is proposed to be erected in a 250 m by 250 m horizontal field at Pulau Ubin and some wind towers will be built. Each wind tower has three rotor blades and the length of each blade is 40 m.

parts.text:
According to building regulations, the minimum distance between two wind towers, measured from the foot of one tower to another, has to be five times the length of a rotor blade.
An engineer made a suggestion on how to arrange five wind towers $W_{1},\ W_{2},\ W_{3},\ W_{4}$ and $W_{5}$ in a square field. The arrangement is shown in the diagram below, with $W_{1},\ W_{2},\ W_{4},\ W_{5}$ at the four corners and $W_{3}$ at the centre.
Explain why the engineer's suggestion does not meet the building regulations. Support your answer with working.
parts.label: a
parts.answer: The required minimum distance is $5 \times 40 = 200$ m, but a corner tower is only $176.8$ m from the centre tower $W_{3}$, which is less than 200 m. So the arrangement does not meet the regulations.
parts.solution:
Minimum distance required $= 5 \times \text{blade length} = 5 \times 40 = 200$ m.
The distance from a corner tower to the centre tower $W_{3}$ is half the diagonal of the square field. By Pythagoras' Theorem:
$$\text{diagonal} = \sqrt{250^{2} + 250^{2}} = \sqrt{125\,000} = 353.55\ldots \text{ m}$$
$$W_{1}W_{3} = \frac{353.55}{2} = 176.8 \text{ m (1 d.p.)}$$
Since $176.8 \text{ m} < 200 \text{ m}$, the distance from each corner tower to $W_{3}$ is less than the required minimum.
$\therefore$ the engineer's suggestion does not meet the building regulations.
(The side distances $W_{1}W_{2} = W_{1}W_{4} = 250$ m are acceptable; it is only the four distances to the centre that fail.)

parts.text:
Singapore wants to estimate the cost savings from generating electricity through this wind station. The formula $C = -10y^{2} + 90y - 130$ is used to estimate the cost savings in $C$ million dollars during the first $y$ years of operation.
This formula can be re-written as $C = a(y - n)^{2} + m$ where it will take $n$ years to achieve the maximum cost savings of $m$ million dollars. Find the maximum cost savings and the number of years it will take to achieve this.
parts.label: b
parts.answer: It takes 4.5 years to achieve a maximum cost savings of 72.5 million dollars.
parts.solution:
Complete the square:
$$C = -10y^{2} + 90y - 130$$
$$= -10(y^{2} - 9y) - 130$$
$$= -10\left[(y - 4.5)^{2} - 4.5^{2}\right] - 130$$
$$= -10(y - 4.5)^{2} + 10(20.25) - 130$$
$$= -10(y - 4.5)^{2} + 202.5 - 130$$
$$= -10(y - 4.5)^{2} + 72.5$$
So $a = -10$, $n = 4.5$ and $m = 72.5$.
Since $-10(y - 4.5)^{2} \leq 0$, the greatest value of $C$ is $72.5$, occurring when $y = 4.5$.
$\therefore$ it takes 4.5 years to achieve a maximum cost savings of 72.5 million dollars.

stem: A hot water tank, shown in Diagram I, is made by joining a hemisphere of radius 30 cm to an open cylinder of radius 30 cm and height 70 cm. The tank is full of water.

parts.text: Calculate the volume of water, in litres, that the tank can contain.
parts.label: a
parts.solution:
The tank is a cylinder topped by a hemisphere, both of radius 30 cm.
$$V_{\text{cylinder}}=\pi r^2h=\pi(30)^2(70)=63\,000\pi\text{ cm}^3$$
$$V_{\text{hemisphere}}=\frac{2}{3}\pi r^3=\frac{2}{3}\pi(30)^3=18\,000\pi\text{ cm}^3$$
$$V_{\text{total}}=63\,000\pi+18\,000\pi=81\,000\pi=254\,469.0\text{ cm}^3$$
Convert to litres using $1\text{ litre}=1000\text{ cm}^3$:
$$V=\frac{254\,469.0}{1000}=254.469\approx 254\text{ litres (3 s.f.)}$$

parts.text: Calculate the total surface area, including the base, of the outside of the tank.
parts.label: b
parts.solution:
The outside consists of the curved surface of the cylinder, the flat circular base, and the curved surface of the hemisphere. (The cylinder is open at the top, where the hemisphere joins it, so no extra circle is counted there.)
$$\text{Curved surface of cylinder}=2\pi rh=2\pi(30)(70)=4200\pi$$
$$\text{Base}=\pi r^2=\pi(30)^2=900\pi$$
$$\text{Curved surface of hemisphere}=2\pi r^2=2\pi(30)^2=1800\pi$$
$$\text{Total}=4200\pi+900\pi+1800\pi=6900\pi$$
$$=21\,676.99\ldots\approx 21\,700\text{ cm}^2\text{ (3 s.f.)}$$

parts.text: All of the water from the tank runs into a bath, shown in Diagram II, which it just completely fills. The bath is a prism whose cross-section is a trapezium. The lengths of the parallel sides of the trapezium are 0.4 m and 0.6 m. The depth of the bath is 0.3 m. Calculate the length of the bath, in metres.
parts.label: c
parts.solution:
Cross-sectional area of the trapezium:
$$A=\frac{1}{2}(a+b)h=\frac{1}{2}(0.4+0.6)(0.3)=0.15\text{ m}^2$$
Convert the volume of water to cubic metres using $1\text{ m}^3=1\,000\,000\text{ cm}^3$:
$$V=254\,469.0\text{ cm}^3=0.2544690\text{ m}^3$$
For a prism, $V=A\times \ell$, so
$$\ell=\frac{V}{A}=\frac{0.2544690}{0.15}=1.6964\ldots$$
$$\ell\approx 1.70\text{ m (3 s.f.)}$$

stem: Write down a possible equation for each of the graphs below. In each case, select one of the equations from the box above.

parts.text: Graph (a).
parts.label: a
parts.solution:
The curve has the shape of a cubic that falls from left to right and cuts the $y$-axis at $2$.
A negative coefficient of $x^{3}$ gives that shape, and the constant term gives the intercept:
$y = 2 - 3x^{3}$

parts.text: Graph (b).
parts.label: b
parts.solution:
The curve lies entirely above the $x$-axis, falls steeply and flattens towards the axis — exponential decay.
$y = \dfrac{1}{5^{x}}$  (i.e. $y = 5^{-x}$)

parts.text: Graph (c).
parts.label: c
parts.solution:
The graph is a hyperbola in two opposite quadrants with the axes as asymptotes.
The negative constant puts the branches in the second and fourth quadrants:
$y = -\dfrac{2}{x}$

stem: A flag pole with Flag A is attached to a pillar by a rope of length 21 cm, as shown in the diagram.

parts.text: Find $\angle PQR$, the angle between the pole of Flag A and the wall.
parts.label: a
parts.solution:
In $\triangle PQR$, $\angle QRP = 90^\circ$, $QR = 20$ cm and $RP = 21$ cm.
$\tan \angle PQR = \frac{21}{20}$
$\angle PQR = \tan^{-1}\frac{21}{20} = 46.397^\circ$
$\angle PQR = 46.4^\circ$ (1 d.p.)

parts.text: A flag pole with Flag B, which is longer than that of Flag A, is fixed to the wall at the same angle. Given that $\angle SQT$ is equal to $\angle PQR$, without the use of a calculator, write down the value of $\tan \angle SQT$ and suggest a reason for your answer.
parts.label: b
parts.answer: $\tan \angle SQT = \frac{21}{20}$, because $\angle SQT = \angle PQR$ and equal angles have equal tangents.
parts.solution:
$\tan \angle SQT = \tan \angle PQR = \frac{21}{20}$
Reason: $\angle SQT$ is given to be equal to $\angle PQR$, and equal angles have equal tangent ratios. (Equivalently, $\triangle QST$ is an enlargement of $\triangle QRP$, so the ratio of opposite side to adjacent side is unchanged.)

parts.text: The vertical distance between the top of both ropes is 10 cm. Find $ST$, the length of rope attaching the pole of Flag B to the pillar.
parts.label: c
parts.solution:
In $\triangle PQR$ (right-angled at $R$):
$PQ = \sqrt{20^{2} + 21^{2}} = \sqrt{841} = 29$ cm
$T$ is 10 cm above $P$ on the pillar, so $QT = QP + PT = 29 + 10 = 39$ cm.
In $\triangle QST$, $\angle QST = 90^\circ$ and $\angle SQT = 46.397^\circ$.
$ST = QT \sin \angle SQT = 39 \sin 46.397^\circ = 28.24$
$ST = 28.2$ cm (3 s.f.)

stem:
Figure 1 shows a prototype of a drain. It is formed by carving out a prism from a solid cuboid of dimensions $70$ cm by $180$ cm by $50$ cm. The base of the discarded prism is an isosceles trapezium where $FE=CD=x$ cm and $ED=40$ cm.
Figure 2 shows the cross section of the prototype, $ABCDEF$, where the parallel sides of the trapezium $FC$ and $ED$ are parallel to $AB$. The perpendicular distance between $ED$ and $AB$ is $30$ cm.

parts.text: Show that the area of $ABCDEF$ is $2400$ cm$^{2}$.
parts.label: i
parts.solution:
Area of rectangle $ABCF = 70 \times 50 = 3500$ cm$^{2}$
The piece removed is trapezium $FCDE$, with parallel sides $FC=70$ cm and $ED=40$ cm.
Its height $= 50 - 30 = 20$ cm.
Area of $FCDE = \dfrac{1}{2}(70+40)(20) = 1100$ cm$^{2}$
Area of $ABCDEF = 3500 - 1100 = 2400$ cm$^{2}$ (shown)

parts.text: Given that the total surface area of the prototype is $51\,600$ cm$^{2}$, form an equation in $x$ and solve it.
parts.label: ii
parts.solution:
Perimeter of the cross section $ABCDEF$
$= AB + BC + CD + DE + EF + FA$
$= 70 + 50 + x + 40 + x + 50 = 210 + 2x$
Total surface area $= 2 \times \text{cross-sectional area} + \text{perimeter} \times \text{length}$
$51\,600 = 2(2400) + 180(210+2x)$
$51\,600 = 4800 + 37\,800 + 360x$
$51\,600 = 42\,600 + 360x$
$360x = 9000$
$x = 25$

parts.text: Find the volume of cement required to build the prototype, in cm$^{3}$.
parts.label: iii
parts.solution:
The prototype is a prism of cross-sectional area $2400$ cm$^{2}$ and length $180$ cm.
Volume $= 2400 \times 180 = 432\,000$ cm$^{3}$

parts.text: Calculate the cost of cement to build the prototype given that cement costs $\$86.90$ per m$^{3}$, correct your answer to 2 decimal places.
parts.label: iv

stem: Figure 4a shows a wire frame in the shape of a sector $OAB$ with centre $O$ and radius $x\text{ cm}$. Angle $AOB = 75^{\circ}$ and the area of the sector $OAB$ is $128\frac{1}{3}\text{ cm}^{2}$. [Take $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$]

parts.text: Find the value of $x$.
parts.label: i

parts.text: Find the perimeter of sector $OAB$, leaving your answer as a fraction.
parts.label: ii
parts.solution:
$$\text{Arc } AB = \frac{75}{360} \times 2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 14 = \frac{5}{24} \times 88 = \frac{55}{3}\text{ cm}$$
$$\text{Perimeter} = OA + OB + \text{arc } AB = 14 + 14 + \frac{55}{3} = \frac{84 + 55}{3} = \frac{139}{3} = 46\frac{1}{3}\text{ cm}$$

parts.text: The wire frame is then reshaped to form an isosceles trapezium, $PQRS$, as shown in Figure 4b. It is given that $PS = QR = 6\text{ cm}$, $PQ$ is parallel to $SR$ and the length of $PQ$ is equal to the radius of the sector in Figure 4a. Show that the shortest distance between $PQ$ and $SR$ is 5.096 cm, correct to 4 significant figures.
parts.label: iii
parts.solution:
The same wire is used, so the perimeter of $PQRS$ equals the perimeter of the sector, $\frac{139}{3}$ cm. Also $PQ = 14$ cm.
$$SR = \frac{139}{3} - 14 - 6 - 6 = \frac{139 - 78}{3} = \frac{61}{3}\text{ cm}$$
Drop perpendiculars from $P$ and $Q$ to $SR$. By symmetry the horizontal overhang at each end is
$$\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{61}{3} - 14\right) = \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{19}{3} = \frac{19}{6}\text{ cm}$$
By Pythagoras' Theorem, the perpendicular distance $h$ satisfies
$$h^{2} = 6^{2} - \left(\frac{19}{6}\right)^{2} = 36 - \frac{361}{36} = \frac{935}{36}$$
$$h = \frac{\sqrt{935}}{6} = 5.09629\ldots = 5.096\text{ cm (4 s.f.)}\quad\text{(shown)}$$

parts.text: Hence, find the area of trapezium $PQRS$.
parts.label: iv
parts.solution:
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2}(PQ + SR) \times h = \frac{1}{2}\left(14 + \frac{61}{3}\right) \times 5.09629\ldots$$
$$= \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{103}{3} \times 5.09629\ldots = 87.486\ldots$$
$$= 87.5\text{ cm}^{2} \text{ (3 s.f.)}$$

stem: The diagram shows a pentagon, $ABCDE$, with all sides of length $3$ cm. Two of the interior angles are each $90^\circ$.

parts.text: Show that angle $ADB$ is $41.41^\circ$.
parts.label: i
parts.solution: $AD = BD = \sqrt{3^2 + 3^2} = \sqrt{18}$ cm. In $\triangle ADB$ with $AB = 3$: $3^2 = 18 + 18 - 2(18)\cos\angle ADB$; $\cos\angle ADB = \dfrac{18+18-9}{2(18)} = \dfrac{27}{36}$; $\angle ADB = 41.41^\circ$ (shown).

parts.text: Find the area of the pentagon $ABCDE$.
parts.label: ii

parts.text: The diagram also shows a container in the shape of an inverted pyramid. The open end of the container is the pentagon $ABCDE$. The container has a volume of $60\text{ cm}^3$. Calculate the vertical height, $OX$, of the pyramid.
parts.label: iii
parts.solution: $\text{Volume} = \tfrac{1}{3}\times \text{base area} \times \text{height}$; $60 = \tfrac{1}{3}\times 14.95 \times OX$; $OX = 12.04 = 12.0$ cm (3 s.f.).

parts.text: Water is being poured into the container at the constant rate of $7.5\text{ cm}^3/\text{s}$ until the container is full. On the axes given, sketch the height of the water against time as the container is being filled.
parts.label: iv
parts.answer: Sketch starts at $(0,\ 0)$ and rises concavely (fast at first, slower later as cross-section widens) to the point $(8,\ 12)$, since the container fills in $60 \div 7.5 = 8$ s to a maximum height of $12$ cm.
parts.solution: Time to fill $= \dfrac{60}{7.5} = 8$ seconds. Sketch a curve rising from $(0,0)$ to $(8, 12.0)$, concave downwards (steep at first, then levelling off), since the container is wider near the top.
